item.title: Texas A&M football vs Alabama betting odds: Who's favored in Week 8 clash?
item.description: Texas A&M football is in the midst of a down year, but the Southeastern Conference stops for no program. The Aggies take to the road Saturday to take on Alabama, the 13th-ranked team. The SEC schedule hasn't been kind to A&M (4-3, 1-3). While a win over Citadel brought back some good vibes, the offense's struggles against its peers are well-documented. Quarterback Marcel Reed threw for 189 yards and two interceptions on 19-for-39 passing in a loss to Missouri, and the Aggies are in the bottom half of the conference in offensive yards per game. MORE: What Texas A&M must do to make the CFP Alabama (5-2, 3-2) has hit a bit of a lull after a 5-0 start. Quarterback Keelon Russell struggled against Tennessee, completing 19-of-29 passes for 147 yards and two interceptions in the 27-10 defeat. The Crimson Tide will be without star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, who suffered a knee injury in the loss to the Georgia Bulldogs. Anto Saka of the Texas A&M Aggies celebrates after a tackle in the first half against the Arizona State Sun Devils at Kyle Field on Sept. 12, 2026 in College Station. (Tim Warner/Getty Images) Here are the betting lines for A&M's game against LSU. Texas A&M football vs Alabama betting odds (via BetMGM as of Oct. 22) Spread: Alabama -15 Over/Under: 51.5 Moneyline: A&M +475, Alabama -625 Texas A&M vs Alabama: TV, time Who: Texas A&M Aggies vs. Alabama Crimson Tide What: Week 8 college football When: 2:30 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 26 Where: Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Ala. TV channel: ABC Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. item.title: Houston Christian at Lamar: How to watch, date, time, TV channel
item.description: Houston Christian goes for its third straight win as it takes on Lamar in a Southland Conference matchup. (Michael Wade/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Houston Christian makes a short road trip in search of its third consecutive win. The Huskies (4-3, 3-1 Southland) will trek to Beaumont for a Saturday afternoon kickoff against Lamar (5-2, 3-1). While HCU used a big fourth quarter to get past East Texas A&M last week, Lamar - which is ranked 16th in the Stats FCS Top 25 - saw its winning streak end at four games with a 34-31 loss to Southeastern Louisiana. The teams have played just twice before, with the road team winning each time. They last played in 2023 in Houston, a 21-19 Lamar victory. Houston Christian at Lamar When: 3 p.m. Saturday Where: Provost Umphrey Stadium, Beaumont TV: ESPN+ Radio: 920 AM 2026 Houston Christian football schedule Aug. 27: beat Southeastern La., 34-28 Sept. 5: lost to Rice, 31-3 Sept. 12: beat Arkansas Baptist, 88-0 Sept. 19: lost to Incarnate Word, 30-23 (OT) Sept. 26: lost to North Texas, 63-14 Oct. 3: beat Nicholls, 16-2 Oct. 17: beat East Texas A&M, 43-24 Oct. 24: at Lamar, 3 p.m. (ESPN+) Oct. 31: at Stephen F. Austin, 2 p.m. (ESPN+) Nov. 7: vs. McNeese, 4 p.m. (ESPN+) Nov. 14: at Northwestern State, 1 p.m. (ESPN+) Nov. 21: vs. UT Rio Grande Valley, 4 p.m. (ESPN+) Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: Peres Jepchirchir, Olympic and world marathon champ, provisionally suspended in doping case
item.description: PARIS, FRANCE - AUGUST 11: Peres Jepchirchir of Team Kenya competes during the Women’s Marathon on day sixteen of the Olympic Games Paris 2024 at Esplanade Des Invalides on August 11, 2024 in Paris, France. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Getty Images Kenyan Peres Jepchirchir, the Tokyo Olympic gold medalist and 2025 World champion in the marathon, has been provisionally suspended after testing positive for EPO, according to the Athletics Integrity Unit , which handles doping in international track and field. Jepchirchir, 33, tested positive from an out-of-competition sample taken in Kenya before she won the Sydney Marathon on Aug. 30. Athletes can be provisionally suspended before a hearing to determine the final decision in their case. Gianni Demadonna, who is listed as Jepchirchir's athlete representative by World Athletics, said Friday, "I can only say that I feel terrible about what happened and I think it’s only right that an athlete who uses the performance enhancing drugs should be disqualified." Jepchirchir also won major marathons in New York City (2021), Boston (2022) and London (2024).

item.title: Barcelona defender practically ruled out of El Clasico, could return vs Alaves
item.description: Barcelona defender practically ruled out of El Clasico, could return vs Alaves Barcelona are heading into Sunday’s El Clasico against Real Madrid on the back of multiple injury-related absentees. Over the past week, the club have had to deal with injuries to Dani Olmo, Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde. While Garcia and Olmo have both been sidelined for at least a month, there was some hope that Kounde could make it in time for the Clasico as the knock he faced against Real Betis wasn’t so serious. Kounde ruled out vs Real Madrid However, according to AS , Kounde has been practically ruled out for the Clasico on Sunday evening, in yet another major blow for the Blaugrana . Kounde will miss the Real Madrid game. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images) The Frenchman was not seen training with his fellow teammates at Ciutat Esportiva today and it appears he won’t be able to return to full fitness. Kounde was already facing a race against time to be fit for the Real Madrid clash but despite seven day cooling period, the defender has been unable to make it in time. Kounde’s absence leaves Hansi Flick with limited options in defence. Fortunately for the German tactician, Xavi Espart is fit and available after an injury scare during midweek’s defeat to PSG, where he had picked up a knock. Espart is likely to be partnered by Joao Cancelo, Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin in the Barcelona backline. When will Kounde return? Hansi Flick will hope to have Kounde available for the Alaves clash. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Since Kounde is no longer an option for Barcelona against Real Madrid this weekend, the defender has already shifted his focus to getting fit before the club’s next match. Fortunately for Barça, they don’t have to play another Champions League game in midweek, giving Kounde additional time to recover. The French international will be looking to utilise that time to get back to full fitness, just in time for Barcelona’s next game against Alaves on October 31. That is currently the objective for the former Sevilla right-back, who will be looking to utilise injuries to Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia to once again reclaim his place in the starting eleven.

item.title: Stanford’s football pains are myriad
item.description: PALO ALTO, CA - OCTOBER 17: A general view of Stanford Stadium as the Stanford Cardinal attempt a field goal during an NCAA college football game against the Elon Phoenix on October 17, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, California. (Photo by David Madison/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NIL era has not been kind to Stanford football, but then, the years preceding it weren’t so good, either. Stanford hasn’t been to a bowl game since 2018, and other than its 4-2 campaign in 2020, hasn’t finished with a winning record since then either. Stanford’s high admission standards present an extra hurdle for building a competitive roster and they are especially disadvantageous in the portal era. There is also the matter of financial investment, and the Cardinal are lagging behind the bulk of the power four. I wondered if Stanford might emerge in this money era as a heavier spender—surely there is no shortage of money among its alumni base—but the school has answered that question with a resounding no. It seems school’s potential sugar daddies haven’t taken the time out of their busy schedules building tech companies that make society demonstrably worse. The results on the field have been predictable, and this season is another case in point. No advanced stats are necessary to illustrate the myriad problems on display. ( Via Stanford’s game notes .) Stanford has three wins this season: 37-27 over Hawaii (119 in SP+), 34-27 over Georgia Tech (64), and 34-7 over Elon. All three came at home, and the GT game was also a 7:30 p.m. PT kick—the Cardinal are 3-0 in such games against ACC teams from the Eastern time zone, so, uh, there is that. Stanford’s problems on offense are everywhere but boil down to not being able to run the ball that gives it no choice but to rely on a below-average quarterback to get anything done. All five of the Stanford opponents with a pulse have successfully made the Cardinal one-dimensional by limiting it to fewer than 100 yards rushing. In league games, Stanford is averaging 71.5 rushing yards on 2.5 per carry, and has one rushing touchdown. Quarterback Davis Warren leads ACC quarterbacks in pass attempts—Stanford is averaging 37 passes per game in league play—but ranks 12th or worse among ACC QBs in touchdown passes, completion percentage, yards per attempt, and passer rating. The line does a decent job protecting him and he’s only thrown two interceptions in 234 attempts, but this is one of the country’s least explosive offenses and frequently up against it on third downs as a result. Stanford’s defensive radar is more pathetic than NC State’s, which is saying something—the Cardinal is not even vaguely good at anything. In four ACC games, it has surrendered 10 passing touchdowns and 12 rushing touchdowns. ACC opponents have completed 72% of their passes on 9.5 yards per attempt. (Photo by David Madison/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NIL era has not been kind to Stanford football, but then, the years preceding it weren’t so good, either. Stanford’s problems on offense are everywhere but boil down to not being able to run the ball that gives it no choice but to rely on a below-average quarterback to get anything done. All five of the Stanford opponents with a pulse have successfully made the Cardinal one-dimensional by limiting it to fewer than 100 yards rushing. In league games, Stanford is averaging 71.5 rushing yards on 2.5 per carry, and has one rushing touchdown. Quarterback Davis Warren leads ACC quarterbacks in pass attempts—Stanford is averaging 37 passes per game in league play—but ranks 12th or worse among ACC QBs in touchdown passes, completion percentage, yards per attempt, and passer rating. The line does a decent job protecting him and he’s only thrown two interceptions in 234 attempts, but this is one of the country’s least explosive offenses and frequently up against it on third downs as a result. Stanford’s defensive radar is more pathetic than NC State’s, which is saying something—the Cardinal is not even vaguely good at anything. In four ACC games, it has surrendered 10 passing touchdowns and 12 rushing touchdowns. ACC opponents have completed 72% of their passes on 9.5 yards per attempt. They’ve also averaged more than 5.0 yards per rushing attempt against this defense. Stanford has only four sacks in 2026, and two of those came in Week 1 against Hawaii; the Cardinal average fewer than four tackles for loss per game, which is rates 114th nationally. The lack of disruption up front has been disastrous, obviously—and NC State can certainly relate to that. Running a dime-store defense with no playmakers is one thing these teams have in common. There are no excuses for Dave Doeren and NC State in this one. Stanford is the worst team on the schedule not named Richmond, there will be roughly seven people in attendance, and it’s a must-win situation that comes with an extra week of preparation. All of the circumstances are advantageous save the kickoff time. We need to see NC State play like the better team that it is, even with an offensive line held together by Scotch tape.

item.title: Fabian Hurzeler responds to Man United links with strong statement on Brighton future
item.description: Fabian Hurzeler insists he will not “throw away” his impressive work at Brighton to join Manchester United . The German manager, 33, is admired by members of Old Trafford hierarchy due to Brighton’s excellent start to the Premier League season. Brighton sit third, with the Seagulls thrashing the champions Arsenal 3-0 and also knocking United out of the Carabao Cup. Fabian Hurzeler is under contract at Brighton until 2029 (Getty) Hurzeler would sit high on United’s list of replacements if they take the decision to part ways with the under-fire Michael Carrick . United, however, are aware that Hurzeler signed a new long-term contract with Brighton in May, tying him to the club until 2029. It would therefore require another Premier League team to pay a significant compensation fee but Hurzeler believes his work at the club is not finished. “I’m fully focused on my job here,” Hurzeler told a press conference on Friday. “I’ve got no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days. “I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and the job he has done at Manchester United the last season. He's a great human being, a great personality, and I really respect him. “There's nothing more to say about that." Only leaders Manchester City and champions Arsenal have picked up more points than Brighton over the first seven games of the Premier League. They have also scored 23 goals – four more than City, who have the second-most in the league – and have won four in a row in the competition. The Seagulls travel to Liverpool on Sunday and Hurzeler believes his Brighton team can continue to aim high in the Premier League. “I’m really privileged to be here,” Hurzeler said. “I’m part of a journey and I still have this feeling when I go to bed that we are not finished with our journey. Hurzeler said he remains committed to Brighton and does not take their progress for granted (Reuters) “I always emphasise that I’m not 100 per cent satisfied and happy with where we are, there are still improvements to make and potential to get out of the players. “Therefore I really I want to work on that, together with my staff. I have a great group of players, players who support me and give everything for the club. “We have built this [together] over the years. We’ve had good periods, we’ve had bad periods. To build these connections you need time. You don’t take these things for granted. “It’s a people business. Making a people business out of this pressure business is something I don’t take for granted and something I won’t throw away that fast.”

item.title: Guardians News: Vogt Returning. Hedges Departing?
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 19: Manger Stephen Vogt #12 of the Cleveland Guardians walks to the dugout during the fourth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game six of the American League Championship Series at Tropicana Field on October 19, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Guardians held their end-of-season press conference featuring Stephen Vogt and Chris Antonetti. Vogt isn’t going to Seattle: "I am committed to being here in Cleveland and I hope I am here for a long time" #Guardians manager Stephen Vogt addresses speculation around potential interest in the Seattle Mariners job #GuardsBall @WEWS pic.twitter.com/RppqH1wAN9 — Mason Horodyski (@MasonHorodyski) October 22, 2026 Antonetti made it sound like Hedges isn’t coming back: "Where things go from here, we have to figure out. But as we told Austin, he put together an extraordinary year, and he not only matched an incredibly an incredible defensive reputation as a catcher, but put together the best offensive season of his career. So, he's earned the… https://t.co/eUCrXQufVJ pic.twitter.com/UgBshpa5QK — Mason Horodyski (@MasonHorodyski) October 22, 2026 Vogt lauded the rookies who led the Guardians: "In talking to all 5 of them and hearing them debrief the season, all they spoke about was 'I can't wait to get back because we're winning it next time'." #Guardians Stephen Vogt on Cleveland's returning rookie core of Parker Messick, Travis Bazzana, Chase DeLauter, Angel Genao… pic.twitter.com/NqRpqslsVC — Mason Horodyski (@MasonHorodyski) October 22, 2026 Vogt tried to assure the media that the team still believes in Tanner Bibee: "He was our rock in that rotation, and I don't see that role changing in '27. He's going to be a big part of our team and a big part of our rotation moving forward" #Guardians Stephen Vogt on Tanner Bibee #GuardsBall @WEWS pic.twitter.com/XMFbCxc0Ql — Mason Horodyski (@MasonHorodyski) October 22, 2026 Antonetti gave the usual company line on free agents Nathaniel Lowe and Foster Griffin: "Both Foster and Nathaniel made massive impact on our team…both guys are free agents, so we'll continue to stay engaged with them over the next few weeks as we develop you know what our off season might look like, and they begin to understand their alternatives." #Guardians … pic.twitter.com/ad2YmsftWt — Mason Horodyski (@MasonHorodyski) October 22, 2026 If you are a Patreon subscriber, Selby is Godcast with Zack Meisel and TJ Zuppe had some interesting insights on the general sense if the Guardians might go after some free agents or trade acquisitions. Seems there is some reason for mild optimism? The World Series starts at 8PM ET tonight.

He's going to be a big part of our team and a big part of our rotation moving forward" #Guardians Stephen Vogt on Tanner Bibee #GuardsBall @WEWS pic.twitter.com/XMFbCxc0Ql — Mason Horodyski (@MasonHorodyski) October 22, 2026 Antonetti gave the usual company line on free agents Nathaniel Lowe and Foster Griffin: "Both Foster and Nathaniel made massive impact on our team…both guys are free agents, so we'll continue to stay engaged with them over the next few weeks as we develop you know what our off season might look like, and they begin to understand their alternatives." #Guardians … pic.twitter.com/ad2YmsftWt — Mason Horodyski (@MasonHorodyski) October 22, 2026 If you are a Patreon subscriber, Selby is Godcast with Zack Meisel and TJ Zuppe had some interesting insights on the general sense if the Guardians might go after some free agents or trade acquisitions. Seems there is some reason for mild optimism? The World Series starts at 8PM ET tonight.

item.title: ‘God Help You If You Cross His Boundaries’ — Dallas Radio Legend Dissects Rumored Tension Between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck at ESPN
item.description: 'God Help You If You Cross His Boundaries' — Dallas Radio Legend Dissects Rumored Tension Between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck Some people never forget a kindness, while also never forgiving someone for crossing a line. Veteran Dallas broadcaster Jody Dean painted that as a portrait of Troy Aikman, comparing the Dallas Cowboys legend to Eagles singer Don Henley. Dean made his remarks while reacting to a report that laid bare just how badly the ESPN broadcasting partners’ relationship had deteriorated. How ESPN’s Troy Aikman-Joe Buck Drama Spilled Into Public View Aikman and Buck’s partnership in the Monday Night Football booth was plastered across headlines after their rumored blowup. Initially, Front Office Sports reported that the two had argued before the Buffalo Bills-Los Angeles Rams game on October 12, and that the issue had been sparked by contract tensions. Since then, “In Touch Weekly” claimed that the argument nearly turned physical. “It nearly got physical off air,” an unnamed source told the magazine. “They were very close to coming to blows.” Puck’s Dylan Byers reported that the relationship had been getting worse even before the contract talks, with one source describing Aikman as “becoming increasingly cold, difficult, short, making comments” toward Buck. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Reacting to this context, Dean wrote , “Troy has always reminded me of another guy I admire: Don Henley.” Henley was one of the founding members of the band “Eagles” and its lead vocalist, delivering hits such as “Hotel California” and “Life in the Fast Lane.” Dean continued: “He’ll go out of his way to do something kind and swear you to secrecy over it, but God help you if you cross his boundaries; and he doesn’t ever forget.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Buck finalized a six-year ESPN extension reportedly worth more than $100 million, while Aikman has no formal offer from the network. That flips how the pair arrived from Fox in 2022, when ESPN signed Aikman first and then found a way to bring Buck over. Aikman himself addressed the issue in a Dallas radio interview on Oct. 15. “I don’t know that it’s hard to figure out kind of what’s happened,” he said, adding that he would “be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens.” Byers also reported that Aikman felt betrayed that ESPN, Buck and their agency, CAA, kept him in the dark for months while Buck negotiated an early renewal under which the network proposed he might work without Aikman next season. For now, Buck and Aikman are still sharing a booth. They called this week’s Monday Night Football game without any visible sign of the off-camera drama as they build toward calling Super Bowl 61. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: ‘I’m focused on my job’: Hurzeler brushes off Manchester United speculation ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: ‘I’m focused on my job’: Hurzeler brushes off Manchester United speculation ahead of Liverpool clash Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has talked down rumours linking him with the Manchester United job. Hurzeler has been named as a potential options for Manchester United should Michael Carrick lose his job. Manchester United have taken just seven points from seven Premier League games and were thrashed 4-1 by Como in the Champions League in midweek . United are winless in seven games across all competitions. It's a contrast to Hurzeler, whose Brighton side sit third in the table . The Seagulls have won four consecutive Premier League games without conceding, scoring 15 times in the process. Asked about potential interest from Old Trafford, Hurzeler talked down the reports. He said he's focused on success with the Seagulls and said he has 'a lot of respect' for Carrick. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Liverpool, Hurzeler said: "I'm really focused on my job here. I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days and, beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and what he has done with Manchester United the last season. "He's a great human being, a great personality. There's nothing more to say about that." The German was also keen to play down talk of a title challenge. Brighton are the league's leading scorers, and thrashed champions Arsenal 3-0 last month. However, he said it's too soon to speak about his side as title contenders. "No! We go game by game, we try to focus on performance. "Just yesterday I had a conversation with the players and I love the way they are thinking. They said 'we don't want to focus on results, we want to focus on performances and how we get better, how we can improve because then the results will come'. "Then we can speak at the end of the season about where we are, where we should have been. But now it is solution-focused, process-orientated and trying to get the best out of the players."

item.title: Fly ball: A look at Rays and Brewers jewelry ahead of World Series
item.description: No matter who wins the 2026 World Series, one team will be getting their first championship rings. But whether the Tampa Bay Rays or Milwaukee Brewers win the Fall Classic, bling continued to be a part of baseball this season. The Rays, who have a penchant for pizzazz, beat the Cleveland Guardians in the American League Championship Series to punch their ticket to the World Series. On their journey to the championship matchup, Milwaukee swept the Los Angeles Dodgers , who dominated the fashion game last postseason, in the National League Championship Series. While the baseball world has been hesitant to embrace displays of personal expression like the bat flip or tilted caps , jewelry is the way that players have shown their style. Ahead of Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, Oct. 23, here is a brief look at this season's jewelry for the two teams in the World Series and other sartorial highlights from the past: Tampa Bay Rays jewelry for World Series Van Cleef & Arpels continues to be a favorite jewelry brand among baseball players. On the Rays, Junior Caminero wears a long double-stranded Alhambra necklace featuring the brand's signature clovers. The third baseman completes his look with a pair of dangly earrings that make his celebrations extra lively. "TAMPAAA ... THIS IS FOR YOU" - Junior Caminero pic.twitter.com/yHx8y4xBoz — MLB (@MLB) October 20, 2026 Caminero's Tampa Bay teammate, Yandy Díaz, has long been known to wear jewelry while playing. In fact, back in 2019, he had a massive gold rope chain that went with him all the way to the American League Division Series. There was even a Twitter account dedicated to the shiny accessory. This year, Díaz played with layers of gold chains around his neck. Two necklaces had large charms, one was a spider based on his nickname, "Arañita," and the other was his No. 2 in a scope. Milwaukee Brewers World Series jewelry For the Brewers, Jackson Chourio holds it down in the swag department. The outfielder wears a chunky gold interlocking chain that hangs just around his neck. Milwaukee pitcher Trevor Megill also adds some flair to his game day look. He wears two simple gold chains that flow with his movements. Los Angeles Dodgers 2025 World Series jewelry Last season, the Dodgers stormed the fashion world with their accessory game. Fashion content creator Jack Savoie became the go-to expert in breaking down the drip. Miguel Rojas wore blue jewelry from Van Cleef & Arpels' Alhambra collection en route to Los Angeles' World Series victory. He not only had a necklace with the blue charms, but also had matching earrings. This year, Rojas continued to show off his style. At media day, he was a reporter for MLB Español and interviewed members of the Rays and Brewers as they got ready for their chance to hoist the Commissioner's Trophy. Ahead of Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, Oct. 23, here is a brief look at this season's jewelry for the two teams in the World Series and other sartorial highlights from the past: Tampa Bay Rays jewelry for World Series Van Cleef & Arpels continues to be a favorite jewelry brand among baseball players. On the Rays, Junior Caminero wears a long double-stranded Alhambra necklace featuring the brand's signature clovers. The third baseman completes his look with a pair of dangly earrings that make his celebrations extra lively. "TAMPAAA ... THIS IS FOR YOU" - Junior Caminero pic.twitter.com/yHx8y4xBoz — MLB (@MLB) October 20, 2026 Caminero's Tampa Bay teammate, Yandy Díaz, has long been known to wear jewelry while playing. In fact, back in 2019, he had a massive gold rope chain that went with him all the way to the American League Division Series. There was even a Twitter account dedicated to the shiny accessory. This year, Díaz played with layers of gold chains around his neck. Two necklaces had large charms, one was a spider based on his nickname, "Arañita," and the other was his No. 2 in a scope. Milwaukee Brewers World Series jewelry For the Brewers, Jackson Chourio holds it down in the swag department. The outfielder wears a chunky gold interlocking chain that hangs just around his neck. Milwaukee pitcher Trevor Megill also adds some flair to his game day look. He wears two simple gold chains that flow with his movements. Los Angeles Dodgers 2025 World Series jewelry Last season, the Dodgers stormed the fashion world with their accessory game. Fashion content creator Jack Savoie became the go-to expert in breaking down the drip. Miguel Rojas wore blue jewelry from Van Cleef & Arpels' Alhambra collection en route to Los Angeles' World Series victory. He not only had a necklace with the blue charms, but also had matching earrings. This year, Rojas continued to show off his style. At media day, he was a reporter for MLB Español and interviewed members of the Rays and Brewers as they got ready for their chance to hoist the Commissioner's Trophy. The infielder wore huggie earrings in his ears and his monstrous World Series ring on his finger. During the 2025 World Series, Rojas wasn't the only Dodgers player to catch the attention of style experts with his accessories. Pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto dazzled in a sapphire tennis necklace. Mookie Betts has also worn strings of necklaces throughout his career, including one with a charm of a baseball bat. His swagger was on full display during the championship series. Joc Pederson's pearls at 2021 World Series Joc Pederson's pearls put a stamp on MLB fashion in a major way for the 2021 World Series when he won the title with the Atlanta Braves. And it wasn't just a strand of small pearls. Per Sports Illustrated , compared to the average size 8-millimeter pearls, Pederson's were nearly double the size at 14 millimeters each. The necklace, which was crafted by Happy Jewelers, created such a buzz that the Braves sold replicas for $5. After the season, the real one was sent to the Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, New York. As for his inspiration for the fashion statement, Pederson said, "I just saw the pearls and I was, like, you know what? That looks cool." Ken Griffey Jr., Deion Sanders influenced baseball fashion There are several other players who have influenced baseball fashion through their accessories. Back in the 2000s, Ken Griffey Jr. became known for wearing his baseball cap backwards, but added some flair to his uniform with diamond earrings and a silver chain. Deion Sanders is among the most influential figures in all of sports fashion. He is responsible for the phrase, "Look good, feel good, play good," and, although he's primarily known for his swagger in the world of football, he wore large necklaces that helped baseball find its fly. item.title: Idi Amin's grandson disqualified for throwing after the bell punch
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Uganda's Aziz Abdul reacts after disqualification in the men's 90+kg quarter-final boxing match against England's Damar Thomas, at the SEC Centre, during day six of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. (is associated with: «Idi Amin's grandson disqualified for throwing after the bell punch») Jane Barlow/PA Wire/dpa Idi Amin's grandson lost his cool again as he crashed to another disqualification defeat in the final of the African Boxing Championships in Nairobi. Aziz Abdul, known as 'Ringo', swung a wild punch at Egypt's Mohamed Hossen after the bell in their men's 90kg final and was instantly thrown out and stripped of his silver medal. Aziz had suffered the same fate at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow in July when he was disqualified for head-butting his English opponent Damar Thomas in their opening bout. The 25-year-old had gone into the bout in Glasgow vowing to become "the new king of Scotland" - a reference to a claim made by his notorious grandfather. Idi Amin became president of Uganda in 1971. During his eight-year reign, hundreds of thousands of people were killed and Amin expelled Uganda's entire Asian population before being deposed and sent into exile. Aziz had raged against the officials following his Commonwealth Games bout and accused organisers of bias and anti-African racism. In his bout in Nairobi, Aziz pulled out of a clinch as the bell sounded then floored Hossen with a punch round the back of his head as his Egyptian opponent turned away. The incident sparked angry scenes involving Hossen's cornermen before Hossen had his arm raised with Aziz having already exited the ring.

item.title: Liverpool Reportedly “Not in Rush” to Extend Mac Allister
item.description: Liverpool FC’s Alexis Mac Allister has probably been the standout midfielder of the season thus far, and it’s a return to form after a very disappointing last season, when pundits and fans alike (me included) questioned whether he had permanently lost the legs and physicality to play in the Premier League. In Liverpool beat reporter Dominic King’s new piece for the Telegraph , he had this to say at the end about Mac’s potential new deal: “Liverpool are not in any rush to start talking about new contracts with Mac Allister, who they were able to sign on a cut-price £35m deal in June 2023, but if he keeps playing with this zip, he can change that situation too.“ The 27-year-old midfielder had expressed his thoughts about not being offered a new deal earlier this season: “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very, very sad,” he told reporters on Tuesday. Everyone can see I give 100 percent for this football club, every single day in training, games. “ “Of course, I can have very good games, bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best. I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts, and that makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I didn’t get mine.” The chance of a Mac Allister extension after last season was close to zero, and Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch were obviously extended because they’re younger than Mac. However, in a strange twist of fate, the Argentinian has been playing the best of those three this season, and his fit as Andoni Iraola continues to try to find his best lineup combination in the middle of the park, despite injuries and suspensions, has been the easiest. He’s the best passer out of the trio (although Trey Nyonyi is knocking on his door) and offers something in both boxes. Mac had this to say after the Villarreal game, noting the difference between this and last season: “The way we play it is quite different. I don’t like to compare. I’m feeling good right now, that’s what I want, and that’s what I enjoy. From the first day we started working together, I saw something really important .“ “I think we are going in the right direction but if you look at the game today, it was far from perfect so we need to work, keep giving everything. It’s a really important year for us so hopefully we can win some trophies.” I think the general populace always wants to see players who want to play for the club rewarded. I would not be opposed to a Mac Allister extension, but there are factors that work for and against him. With rumours of a midfielder addition in the upcoming winter and summer transfer windows, we’ll have to see how it plays out.

item.title: The next two weeks will determine Shane Steichen’s future with the Colts
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts looks on against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts made a major decision when the Irsays chose to part ways with 10-year general manager Chris Ballard. It was a long time coming, but if things don’t shape up quickly, it won’t be the last move made in 2026. When it rains, it pours, and Shane Steichen better have his umbrella and poncho on because he is in danger of being the next to fall. The next two weeks could very well determine his fate. Offensively, the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings are one of the worst undefeated teams ever. They don’t put up a lot of yards or points. That’s all the good news there is for the Colts, though. As statistically bad as they may be on offense, they are coming off a bye, are at home, and have one of the league’s best defenses. Kyler Murray is back under center and is starting to get comfortable. In the building in which the Colts surrendered a 33-0 lead, anything is possible, but being a touchdown underdog implies this will be an uphill climb. If Steichen can rally the troops in the face of adversity and win, he can take a breath. It will only be a small gulp, however, because the test continues in Jacksonville against the Jaguars. Their record doesn’t matter. Whether Trevor Lawrence has his team rolling doesn’t matter. Great or horrible, the Colts don’t win in Jacksonville anymore. If Steichen wants to keep his job, this has to be the year to break the curse. These are two tough games to get the mojo back. Shane Steichen can script the first twenty or so plays, but after that, it falls apart. The Colts have already shown what “Find a Way” means when they released Ballard. It means win. Nothing else. Steichen’s leash was short to begin the year, and he is officially on notice as the next one on the chopping block. If he loses both, he will most likely be gone. This is a results-oriented league. Steichen must show those results or be shown the door.

item.title: Man Utd loanee Andre Onana rushed to hospital after horror multi-car crash in Turkey
item.description: FBL-EUR-C3-FERENCVAROS-TRABZONSPOR - AFP Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana, currently spending the season on loan in the Turkish Super Lig, was reportedly involved in a serious road accident on Thursday night. The Cameroon international was taken to a local hospital for medical assessment following a frightening high-speed collision involving multiple vehicles. High-speed collision in Trabzon The incident occurred just hours after Onana had helped his temporary side to a clean sheet and a victory over Scottish side Hearts in the Conference League. The celebratory mood quickly turned to concern as the shot-stopper was caught up in a multi-car smash while travelling home from the fixture. Local reports suggest the accident took place on the Yomra road, situated near the Black Sea resort of Trabzon, prompting an immediate response from emergency services. As reported by Daily Star , details emerging from the scene indicate that the crash was a chain-reaction event involving three different vehicles. According to local witnesses and media reports, another car reportedly collided with the rear of Onana’s vehicle at high speed. This initial impact forced the goalkeeper’s car into the vehicle ahead of him, sandwiching the player in a frightening high-speed pile-up that left substantial wreckage scattered across the road. Images and footage circulating on social media following the accident provided a grim visual of the impact. The goalkeeper's car was seen with significant damage to its front wing, while the vehicle that struck him from behind appeared to have a completely crumpled front end. The Cameroon international was taken to a local hospital for medical assessment following a frightening high-speed collision involving multiple vehicles. High-speed collision in Trabzon The incident occurred just hours after Onana had helped his temporary side to a clean sheet and a victory over Scottish side Hearts in the Conference League. The celebratory mood quickly turned to concern as the shot-stopper was caught up in a multi-car smash while travelling home from the fixture. Local reports suggest the accident took place on the Yomra road, situated near the Black Sea resort of Trabzon, prompting an immediate response from emergency services. As reported by Daily Star , details emerging from the scene indicate that the crash was a chain-reaction event involving three different vehicles. According to local witnesses and media reports, another car reportedly collided with the rear of Onana’s vehicle at high speed. This initial impact forced the goalkeeper’s car into the vehicle ahead of him, sandwiching the player in a frightening high-speed pile-up that left substantial wreckage scattered across the road. Images and footage circulating on social media following the accident provided a grim visual of the impact. The goalkeeper's car was seen with significant damage to its front wing, while the vehicle that struck him from behind appeared to have a completely crumpled front end. Official update from Trabzonspor Turkish-Super-League Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan moved quickly to address the growing concerns regarding the player's wellbeing. Speaking to local media outlets, the club chief confirmed the accident had taken place and provided an initial update on the goalkeeper's condition. Dogan stated: “Andre Onana was involved in a road traffic accident earlier this evening. There are no problems with him, and we wish him a speedy recovery.” The 30-year-old was taken to a local medical facility as a precautionary measure following the impact. Medical staff at the hospital were tasked with evaluating the player for potential internal injuries or concussion symptoms that are often associated with high-velocity road accidents. The club has not yet released a secondary medical report confirming when he might be cleared to return to training. Loan spell in Turkey Onana moved to the Super Lig on a temporary basis earlier this season after a mixed start to life at Old Trafford. The move to Trabzonspor was designed to help the former Inter Milan star regain his confidence and consistent playing time away from the intense scrutiny of the Premier League. Before the accident, he had been enjoying a positive run of form, becoming a key figure in the Turkish side's European campaign. His performance against Hearts had been a highlight of his tenure so far, proving his worth to the Turkish giants before the traumatic events on the Yomra road. The goalkeeper has been looking to revitalise a career that saw him become one of the most sought-after keepers in world football during his time at Ajax. This loan spell was viewed as a vital step in proving to Erik ten Hag that he still has a long-term future in Manchester. What comes next for Onana Turkish-Super-League Man Utd officials are expected to be in close contact with their Turkish counterparts to monitor the recovery of their player. While Dogan’s initial statement was optimistic, the physical and psychological toll of such a high-speed collision will need to be carefully assessed. The Red Devils will be keen to ensure their asset receives the best possible care before any decision is made regarding his return to the pitch. The upcoming days will be crucial in determining the full extent of the injuries sustained and how long the Cameroonian will be sidelined from competitive action.

item.title: Luther Burden Just Gave the Bears a Problem Ben Johnson Wants
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after scoring a 24 yard touchdown against the New England Patriots during the second quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears may have discovered that their biggest problem at wide receiver is figuring out how to get Luther Burden III the ball more often. The second-year receiver exploded for 130 yards and a touchdown on four catches against the New England Patriots on Thursday night, and the reaction from quarterback Caleb Williams afterward was telling. Williams didn’t merely praise Burden’s big performance. He called him a “problem child” and made it clear he wants to keep finding ways to get the ball into his hands. That’s an intriguing development for a Bears offense that already has other playmakers to feed. Burden’s breakout raises a bigger question: Has he become too dangerous to remain an occasional weapon? Luther Burden’s Breakout Has the Bears Rethinking His Role Burden’s stat line against New England was eye-catching, but the way he produced those numbers made it even more interesting. All four of his receptions came in the first half, including a 24-yard touchdown on a screen pass with 21 seconds remaining before halftime. The play showcased exactly what makes him different: Once the ball reaches his hands, the defense has a problem. The touchdown wasn’t simply a case of a receiver beating his man downfield. Chicago’s blockers created a path, Burden spotted the opening and accelerated through it. Head coach Ben Johnson highlighted that blocking when discussing the play after the game, praising the receivers and offensive linemen who helped spring Burden into the open field. The Bears’ postgame quotes show that Johnson noticed the collective effort as much as the finish. That matters because Burden’s value isn’t limited to traditional receiver routes. He can turn a short throw into an explosive gain, making him particularly dangerous when Chicago gets the ball to him with room to run. His four catches produced 130 yards, an average of 32.5 yards per reception. The challenge now belongs to Johnson and offensive coordinator Press Taylor. They have a receiver who can change a game on a handful of touches. The question is whether they can create more opportunities without taking the ball away from the other players who make this offense work. Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears may have discovered that their biggest problem at wide receiver is figuring out how to get Luther Burden III the ball more often. Luther Burden’s Breakout Has the Bears Rethinking His Role Burden’s stat line against New England was eye-catching, but the way he produced those numbers made it even more interesting. Chicago’s blockers created a path, Burden spotted the opening and accelerated through it. Head coach Ben Johnson highlighted that blocking when discussing the play after the game, praising the receivers and offensive linemen who helped spring Burden into the open field. The Bears’ postgame quotes show that Johnson noticed the collective effort as much as the finish. That matters because Burden’s value isn’t limited to traditional receiver routes. He can turn a short throw into an explosive gain, making him particularly dangerous when Chicago gets the ball to him with room to run. His four catches produced 130 yards, an average of 32.5 yards per reception. The challenge now belongs to Johnson and offensive coordinator Press Taylor. They have a receiver who can change a game on a handful of touches. The question is whether they can create more opportunities without taking the ball away from the other players who make this offense work. Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) Caleb Williams Is Making His Case for More Luther Burden Williams’ comments after the win offered the clearest indication of how the quarterback views Burden. Calling him a “problem child,” Williams said, “we want to keep getting him the ball in his hands.” He also cited Burden’s perfect 17-for-17 receiving record on throws targeting him so far this season. That is the kind of endorsement that matters. A receiver can have an impressive afternoon, but when his quarterback is openly talking about finding ways to involve him more, it suggests the performance is reinforcing something the offense already believes. Williams also refused to take credit for the touchdown. He pointed instead to the blocking and Burden’s ability to catch the ball, get vertical and finish the play. That humility aside, the connection between the two is becoming increasingly important to Chicago’s offense. Burden isn’t the only young player making noise. Rome Odunze remains a major part of the passing game, while tight end Colston Loveland has also shown he can deliver when called upon. The Bears need all of them. But the beauty of Burden’s skill set is that he can create explosive plays without requiring the offense to build every possession around him. As NBC Sports’ interview with Burden illustrates, the receiver has been discussing his development under Johnson and his connection with Williams. Thursday’s performance gave that conversation a compelling new dimension. Ben Johnson Has Been Betting on Burden for Months Williams’ enthusiasm didn’t emerge out of nowhere. Johnson was praising Burden long before Thursday night’s breakout. In May, the coach said, “I’m buying Luther Burden stock right now,” after seeing the receiver’s improvement during the offseason program. Johnson pointed to his approach to practice, his finishing ability and the explosive plays he was producing. At the NFL owners meetings in March, Johnson said he wanted to get the ball into Burden’s hands “as often as we possibly can.” The Bears’ official report made clear that the coaching staff already viewed him as a dynamic playmaker with outstanding yards-after-catch ability. Now the production is catching up with the praise. That doesn’t guarantee Burden will suddenly receive a huge increase in targets every week, and one big performance doesn’t settle his place in the receiver rotation. But the combination of Johnson’s long-standing belief and Williams’ postgame comments makes this more than a one-night story. The Bears have a young receiver who can turn ordinary plays into extraordinary gains. They don’t need to force-feed him the ball or redesign the offense around him. They do need to find ways to make opposing defenses account for him on every possession. If Thursday was a glimpse of what Burden can become, Chicago may have found another weapon capable of making its offense far more dangerous. And if Williams gets his way, the “problem child” won’t be disappearing from the game plan anytime soon. item.title: Marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir suspended after positive EPO test
item.description: Reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir has been suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) after testing positive for EPO. The 33-year-old returned an adverse analytical finding for the performance-enhancing drug in a sample taken in Kenya before her victory at the Sydney Marathon this August. The AIU announced it had provisionally suspended Jepchirchir in a statement released on Friday, just a day after Ethiopia’s former Tokyo Marathon winner Ruti Aga was given a six-year ban by the agency for a positive test for methylprednisolone and tampering with the investigation. Kenyan Jepchirchir is a four-time World Marathon Major winner and claimed Olympic gold in the marathon at Tokyo 2020. She won the world marathon title for the first time in Tokyo last September, adding to her two individual half-marathon world titles, and is both a former world record holder in the half-marathon and a former women’s-only world record holder in the marathon, set when she won in London in 2024. She withdrew from this year’s London Marathon due to a stress fracture sustained after finishing second in the Valencia marathon last December, making her return to top-level competition in Sydney. She is currently fifth in the world rankings. More follows

item.description: No. 11 Tennessee visits South Carolina as a 2.5-point underdog to headline college football ’s Week 8 upset watch, one of six games where the underdog carries a credible path to an outright win. The Volunteers (6-1) beat Alabama 26-10 last week and have lost only to Texas, while South Carolina (3-3) comes off a bye after a 38-19 win at Florida. Each game in the upset watch gets a grade from 1 to 10, and six more games get shorter grades at the bottom. A win would make the Falcons bowl-eligible, but they haven’t won in Laramie since 2012. Wyoming (4-3, 3-1) has won two straight behind quarterback Tyler Hughes, who ran for four touchdowns in a 41-23 win over Northern Illinois. Cowboys coach Jay Sawvel tied this matchup to drive length. “In the last nine times that we’ve played Air Force, if they have four drives of eight or more plays, we’ve only won one game ,” Sawvel said. Sawvel also wants his defense to put the Falcons in third-and-long as often as possible, though Air Force has converted 13 of 15 fourth downs this season. Wyoming ranks 118th nationally in adjusted EPA per play on defense, so the Cowboys need a short game decided on one late possession. Air Force’s option attack controls the clock enough to win, but a five-point margin makes the moneyline a better play than laying 5.5. West Virginia’s defense gives up too many big plays to win in Fort Worth, but an offense that snaps the ball this fast creates enough extra possessions to stay within 10.5 points. Picks: TCU 31-27, West Virginia +10.5, Over 57.5 Tennessee (+2.5) at South Carolina: Upset Watch 8 Tennessee coach Josh Heupel during a football game against Alabama at Neyland Stadium | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kickoff: Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET (ESPN) No. 11 Tennessee (6-1, 3-1 SEC) beat Alabama 26-10 last week, and its only loss came by three points against Texas. George MacIntyre is expected to make his third straight start at quarterback, while running back DeSean Bishop carried the offense with 32 carries against the Crimson Tide. South Carolina (3-3, 1-3) had a bye after the win at Florida, where LaNorris Sellers threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. “The way that LaNorris is seeing the field and doing things right now, he’s able to get the ball to whoever’s open ,” Gamecocks coach Shane Beamer said. Vols coach Josh Heupel pointed to the extra rest, saying, “A big part of this test is they’ve got two weeks of preparation .” Tennessee’s defense ranks 15th nationally in adjusted EPA per play, compared with 72nd for South Carolina. The Gamecocks have already lost home games to Kentucky by one point and Mississippi State by seven. Tennessee wins a low-scoring game with Bishop and its defensive front while MacIntyre avoids mistakes. Picks: Tennessee 27-21, Tennessee +2.5, Under 50.5 MORE: College fantasy football Week 8 rankings: KJ Duff, Jahiem White make big jumps Boston College (+5.5) at Georgia Tech: Upset Watch 7 BC Eagles quarterback Mason McKenzie (10) throws a pass against the Pittsburgh Panthers | Eric Canha-Imagn Images Kickoff: Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET (ACC Network) Boston College (3-3, 1-2 ACC) beat Pittsburgh 27-21 for its first conference win, and quarterback Mason McKenzie threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Tech (2-4, 1-2) lost 34-24 at Virginia Tech and has dropped two of its last three games. Yellow Jackets coach Brent Key built his scouting report around the former Division II quarterback, saying McKenzie “extends plays, scrambles, avoids pressure.” Key also had a blunt message for his own team. “ If you want to be consistent, go be consistent . Go do it,” Key said. Georgia Tech may also be without captain Jordan Walker , who is working back from ankle surgery. The Eagles allow 169.3 passing yards per game, 18th nationally, and they’ve forced 11 turnovers. Georgia Tech sits at minus-4 in turnover margin. BC has scored on only 60% of its red zone trips, but a defense that takes the ball away gives the Eagles enough short fields to win in Atlanta. Picks: Boston College 27-24, Boston College +5.5, Over 50.5 MORE: Week 8 CFB DFS picks: DeSean Bishop headlines DraftKings, FanDuel slates North Dakota State (+4.5) at New Mexico: Upset Watch 5 Kickoff: Saturday, Oct. 24, 10 p.m. ET (The CW) North Dakota State (6-1) is in its first FBS season, and its only loss came at UNLV. The Bison have won at Air Force and shut out Wyoming 28-0, while New Mexico (5-1, 2-0 Mountain West) beat Hawaii 21-10 to keep the nation’s top scoring defense at 10.3 points per game. NDSU ranks second. Lobos coach Jason Eck faced the Bison for six seasons as a South Dakota State assistant, and Bison coach Tim Polasek knows it. “Jason Eck is obviously a guy who knows our defensive system very well , he’s faced it multiple times in big moments,” Polasek said. Eck singled out Bison quarterback Nathan Hayes. “(Hayes) is a big sucker who can throw it well and move,” Eck said. New Mexico also leads FBS with 13 interceptions, and that secondary makes long Bison drives difficult. NDSU’s defense keeps the score low and the game close, but the Lobos win at home with one more scoring drive. item.title: Could The Manchester City Scandal Overshadow Brighton’s EPL Fairy Tale?
item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - JANUARY 07: Erling Braut Haaland of Manchester City scores their side's first goal from the penalty spot, his 150th for Manchester City in all competition, during the Premier League match between Manchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion at Etihad Stadium on January 07, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images) Getty Images Every gripping story needs a villain. A common evil that those perceived as more righteous can aim to overcome for the greater good. Well, for the most part anyway. Because while Batman needs The Joker and James Bond basks in the glory of besting a menagerie of sociopathic tyrants, the last thing the English Premier League (EPL) wanted was for Manchester City to emerge on the dark side of its narrative. When the Cityzens were found guilty of 114 charges for various rule breaches in September – a ruling the EPL league leaders vehemently disputes and have appealed – the club became English soccer’s persona non grata. According to rival fans, City is now a disgraced former champion, a scandal that threatens to undermine all competition until the club receives punishment. Yet, Enzo Maresca’s team keeps on winning. A perfect record of seven wins from seven games at the start of this new league campaign leaves it clear at the top of the table, arguably making things even worse for the EPL brand. Is Man City genuinely in the title race? Are the points the side is earning more likely to help in a relegation battle post-points deduction? Does any of the sport being offered up mean anything? The worst-case scenario could even be unfolding behind. After an excellent start to the season, Brighton sits in third place, only a matter of points off the pace. The Seagulls have outscored everyone else in the division and have the joint-best defensive record, with some pundits suggesting that good results against Liverpool on Sunday and City the following weekend would mark them out as potential champions. Building a sustained title challenge would be impressive in itself. The club has never won an English league championship in its 125-year history, with a best-ever EPL finish of sixth a few years ago. But what if it genuinely can carry the fight throughout the season, but ultimately finish second to City, only for a points deduction to be applied soon afterwards? It’s a scenario that’s not completely unrealistic. If Man City’s appeal is rejected and a severe points punishment is imposed next spring or summer, Brighton could be awarded a title that couldn’t be celebrated on the pitch or in the stands. A great achievement that would somehow be tainted by actions beyond the club’s control. What would make it worse is that Brighton is held up as a bastion of sustainable club ownership. The Seagulls have outscored everyone else in the division and have the joint-best defensive record, with some pundits suggesting that good results against Liverpool on Sunday and City the following weekend would mark them out as potential champions. Building a sustained title challenge would be impressive in itself. The club has never won an English league championship in its 125-year history, with a best-ever EPL finish of sixth a few years ago. But what if it genuinely can carry the fight throughout the season, but ultimately finish second to City, only for a points deduction to be applied soon afterwards? It’s a scenario that’s not completely unrealistic. If Man City’s appeal is rejected and a severe points punishment is imposed next spring or summer, Brighton could be awarded a title that couldn’t be celebrated on the pitch or in the stands. A great achievement that would somehow be tainted by actions beyond the club’s control. What would make it worse is that Brighton is held up as a bastion of sustainable club ownership. A team backed up by owner Tony Bloom’s Jamestown Analytics, which uses a top-secret data algorithm to continually unearth talent from some of the globe’s most obscure outposts before selling it on for big money and then reinvesting. It’s a widely admired model that’s the envy of many modern-day soccer clubs. The story of Brighton winning the EPL wouldn’t have the luster of Leicester City’s out-of-nowhere 5,000-1 shot success of 2016, but it would highlight a different story of gradual growth that has landed a traditionally lower-league club in with the elite. It’s a tale the EPL brand would benefit from basking in, giving clubs at every level renewed hope. Yet there’s an increasing risk that Man City’s ongoing legal battle could overshadow that. City has the right, of course, to challenge what it considers is an incorrect judgement. But that doesn’t prevent collateral damage to the wider soccer brand’s reputation. The story has already cast a pall over the competition’s integrity this season, but should Brighton’s romantic story continue to emerge, it could have even deeper implications. This is a villain the storyline didn’t need. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: 11 Days Until Hawkeye Basketball: Kael Combs
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - MARCH 26: Kael Combs #11 of the Iowa Hawkeyes dribbles against the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the second half in the Sweet Sixteen of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Toyota Center on March 26, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Hawkeye football team is set to take on Minnesota tomorrow but it doesn’t mean we can’t dabble in some basketball prep ahead of the first tip-off on November 3rd! Next up is Kael Combs! #11 – Kael Combs, G, 6’4”, 204 lbs 4th year; Nixa, MO; Wyoming/Drake 2025-26: 37 GP, 6.1 PPG, 2.4 RPG, 2.4 APG, 49.1% FG, 33.3% 3P, 83.7% FT, 26.1 MPG (33 starts) With a player like Bennett Stirtz in the starting lineup, finding guys who can fit alongside him is paramount. Combs, who had modest stats at Wyoming and Drake before following Ben McCollum to Iowa, did not have to pedigree of a guy who could be that secondary ball handler with Stirtz. Yet he was a mainstay in Iowa’s lineup with 33 starts and the third most minutes on the team. As the season progressed, the “why” was pretty obvious. He was a tough defender and savvy offensive player who rarely over-indexed on his role. He flashed at times, with a career-high 18 points at Nebraska in the season finale and 16 points in Mackey against Purdue. In the highlights above, he canned an open three and finished around the hoop with a tear drop and a couple tough drives. His last second three sent the game to OT, where the Hawks unfortunately couldn’t finish off the road comeback. It feels like his left-handedness is good for a basket a game as teams forget his dominant hand. The question for Combs becomes – can he turn into the Iron Man PG McCollum typically leans on? In a way, that was answered in Iowa’s 3 tournament wins. He was an iso scorer against Clemson where he notched 15 points as the Tigers sold out to stop Stirtz. He added 11 combined assists in wins against Florida & Nebraska. What we’ve seen so far is the guy who can stir the drink – get Iowa into its offense, drive and finish or kick out to another open Hawkeye, play tough consistent defense. In other words: Steady Eddy. Given the talent Iowa brings back around Combs, that might be all the Hawks need to have a successful season. But if goes from a 6 PPG, 2 APG guy to something like 14 PPG/6 APG, it raises the ceiling substantially on what this team might be able to accomplish.

item.title: Dolphins news: Pending free agents, Jets preview, and trade rumors
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: JuJu Brents #8 of the Miami Dolphins exits the field after warmups prior to an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are coming out of their Week 6 bye hoping to mark their first win of the season as they face the New York Jets this weekend. Miami’s immediate focus is to put together a full game and turn flashes of competitiveness into consistency. The longer-term focus has the coaching staff and front office considering which players from this rebuild will remain with the team in 2027 and beyond. Miami has 22 players on expiring contracts this season, and Miami Dolphins on SI writer Alain Poupart took a look at who could be playing themselves into a contract extension as well as players who are likely to hit the free agent market after the season. For the four most likely free agents to return, Poupart starts with a veteran at a position everyone expected to be a weak point for the Dolphins this season: CB JuJu Brents — This is a player the Dolphins should prioritize because he still continues to perform at a high level and plays a premium position. The ability to stay healthy has been the issue so far in Brents’ career, but he hasn’t missed a game yet (knock on wood) so far in 2026. As for a player who might be allowed to leave in free agency, Poupart started his list of four with a name many fans could have guessed: T Austin Jackson — Despite his poor Pro Football Focus standing (he’s dead last among all NFL tackles), Jackson is a solid veteran tackle who’s simply off to a bad start. The issue with Jackson is how it would cost to bring him back in what probably wouldn’t be a starting role and whether he even would be interested in that idea after being asked to take a pay cut this year. item.title: Nashville SC Shuts Down Austin Streak Behind Schwake’s Strong Debut
item.description: Daniel Jefferson-Imagn Images Nashville SC finally put a stop to Austin FC’s long unbeaten run on Saturday night. The team rolled to a 4-1 victory while rookie goalie Brian Schwake made five crucial saves. This win ends Austin’s eight-match streak without a loss and cements Nashville’s spot in the playoffs. The result shows that even a young keeper can lead a squad to a big win against a tough opponent. According to the Associated Press, Reed Baker-Whiting opened the scoring in the 31st minute after a shot hit the post. Elias Saad doubled the lead in the 67th minute when Austin’s goalie Brad Stuver could not secure a save. Brandon Vázquez pulled one back for Austin in the 76th minute, but Abdul Shakur Mohammed answered right away. Mohammed scored an unassisted goal in the 88th minute and then set up Hany Mukhtar for the final score in stoppage time, according to Yahoo Sports . Why the rookie goalie matters Many people forget that a goalkeeper makes the difference between a close loss and a dominant win. Through his initial 27 MLS starts, Schwake conceded just 22 goals, a remarkable figure for someone so young. The Associated Press noted that he has stepped up when the team needed him most against a dangerous Austin attack. This performance proves that Nashville did not make a mistake trusting a rookie in the net during such a critical game. Nashville has secured a playoff berth and leads the Eastern Conference by 14 points, according to the statistics. They also hold a 10-point lead in the race for the Supporters’ Shield. Austin, on the other hand, falls to 4-4-6 at home and saw their unbeaten run end on Saturday. The gap between these two teams is growing, and Nashville’s road record now stands at 6-3-5. Austin needs to find answers fast Austin FC has too many questions to answer after this loss. They went 3-0-5 during their unbeaten run, but that magic has clearly run out. Stuver made seven saves for Austin, yet it was not enough to stop the flood of goals. The team now faces a tough task to get back on track before the season ends. Nashville has been on a hot streak since the start of August, going 7-1-3 in that span. They followed up big home wins over Chicago Fire and Toronto FC with this solid road victory. The team looks ready to push for the top spot while Austin struggles to find consistency on their home field. The schedule moves quickly for both clubs as they head into midweek action. Nashville will host Sporting Kansas City on Wednesday to keep their momentum going. Austin faces a tough test on the road against Los Angeles FC, also on Wednesday.

item.title: 'Go make them believe': Texas State RB Torrance Burgess Jr. powers nation's top offense
item.description: Texas State running back Torrence Burgess Jr. (4) runs the ball during the game against UIW at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 26, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez) Sometimes, it looks like Texas State football running back Torrance Burgess Jr. is standing still. As the blocks set, he shuffles his feet before bursting through the gap - not the first one that opens, but the right one. Patience is key in the run game, and for Burgess, it's been key for his career. UP NEXT TEXAS STATE VS. UTAH STATE When/where: 6:30 p.m. Saturday in San Marcos. TV: CBS Sports Network. He transferred to Texas State from UTEP in 2024, broke his fibula four games into the 2025 season and had to earn the starter role headed into this season. Through it all, he trusted that his talent would eventually shine, he told the American-Statesman this week. The 5-foot-8, 176-pound back, committed to Tyler Junior College in 2021, and five years and two transfers later, is the nation's second-leading rusher, powering a Texas State offense that ranks No. 1 in yards per game. "It's just something about waiting, right?" former Bobcats running backs coach Barrick Nealy said. "Torrance is reaping the benefits of that." Defining his own career at Texas State Burgess said his high school coach told him his junior year that he wasn't destined for Division I college football. Torrance Burgess Sr. and his wife, Carla, recall sitting with their son, watching a presentation about how his small stature would prevent him from reaching the next level. That day is seared into Burgess' memory. "It was tough at the time, but I was like, 'Nah. I'm not going to let him define my career,'" the younger Burgess said. Texas State running back Torrence Burgess Jr. (4) is tackled by UTSA linebacker Brandon Tucker (23) during the I-35 rivalry college football game at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 12, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Even so, the recruiting sites seemed to agree. Burgess had no FBS interest out of high school. Tyler Junior College and Division II West Texas A&M were his only offers. While Burgess' father wanted him to go to West Texas A&M, something felt off during the visit. When he mentioned potentially betting on himself by going the JUCO route and transferring, the coach dismissed it. "If the D-1s wanted you there, they'd already have you," his coach told him. Texas State running back Torrence Burgess Jr. (4) runs the ball during the game against UIW at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 26, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) The comment struck a nerve, Burgess' father recalled. "TJ," as he calls his son, hates being told he can't do something. But he isn't arrogant. He's confident. Burgess ended up at Tyler Junior College instead in 2021, entering that summer as the team's sixth running back on the depth chart.
