item.content:encoded: Texas State running back Torrence Burgess Jr. (4) runs the ball during the game against UIW at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 26, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez) Sometimes, it looks like Texas State football running back Torrance Burgess Jr. is standing still. As the blocks set, he shuffles his feet before bursting through the gap - not the first one that opens, but the right one. Patience is key in the run game, and for Burgess, it's been key for his career. UP NEXT TEXAS STATE VS. UTAH STATE When/where: 6:30 p.m. Saturday in San Marcos. TV: CBS Sports Network. He transferred to Texas State from UTEP in 2024, broke his fibula four games into the 2025 season and had to earn the starter role headed into this season. Through it all, he trusted that his talent would eventually shine, he told the American-Statesman this week. The 5-foot-8, 176-pound back, committed to Tyler Junior College in 2021, and five years and two transfers later, is the nation's second-leading rusher, powering a Texas State offense that ranks No. 1 in yards per game. "It's just something about waiting, right?" former Bobcats running backs coach Barrick Nealy said. "Torrance is reaping the benefits of that." Defining his own career at Texas State Burgess said his high school coach told him his junior year that he wasn't destined for Division I college football. Torrance Burgess Sr. and his wife, Carla, recall sitting with their son, watching a presentation about how his small stature would prevent him from reaching the next level. That day is seared into Burgess' memory. "It was tough at the time, but I was like, 'Nah. I'm not going to let him define my career,'" the younger Burgess said. Texas State running back Torrence Burgess Jr. (4) is tackled by UTSA linebacker Brandon Tucker (23) during the I-35 rivalry college football game at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 12, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Even so, the recruiting sites seemed to agree. Burgess had no FBS interest out of high school. Tyler Junior College and Division II West Texas A&M were his only offers. While Burgess' father wanted him to go to West Texas A&M, something felt off during the visit. When he mentioned potentially betting on himself by going the JUCO route and transferring, the coach dismissed it. "If the D-1s wanted you there, they'd already have you," his coach told him. Texas State running back Torrence Burgess Jr. (4) runs the ball during the game against UIW at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 26, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) The comment struck a nerve, Burgess' father recalled. "TJ," as he calls his son, hates being told he can't do something. But he isn't arrogant. He's confident. Burgess ended up at Tyler Junior College instead in 2021, entering that summer as the team's sixth running back on the depth chart. He eventually broke out regardless, leading the team with 987 total yards. That's when Texas State coach GJ Kinne, then at Incarnate Word, first noticed Burgess - though he didn't pull the scholarship trigger. Nealy, UTEP's running backs coach at the time, had no such reservations; Burgess joined the Miners in 2022. Nealy played quarterback for Texas State from 2003-05, and Kinne hired him in 2024 as his running back coach. Burgess came with him. Texas State, however, already had first-team all-conference RB Ismail Mahdi and trusted backup Lincoln Pare. Nealy said he asked Burgess' parents to trust him, telling them their son's opportunity would come. "You're going to have these tough conversations," Nealy said. "I remember Carla (Burgess' mother) telling me … ‘Although I don't really understand right now, I trust in the Lord, and I trust you with my son."' Texas State receiver Zachariah Sample (3) celebrates a touchdown by running back Torrence Burgess Jr. (4) during the game against UIW at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 26, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) 'Divine intervention' If Burgess' leg snapped one quarter later against Nicholls in 2025, he wouldn't have been eligible for 2026. NCAA rules at the time stated that an athlete must not have competed in more than 30% of their team's scheduled competitions to qualify for an extra year of eligibility. Because Burgess' injury came in the second quarter of the fourth game, he fell just within that rule. "The way it happened, I feel like it was divine intervention," Burgess' father said. It might've been a blessing in the long term, but the recovery process taxed Burgess mentally, he said. Instead of going to stadiums with his teammates, he spent Saturdays alone at home, grinding through rehab. He seriously considered transferring at the end of the season. Gifted another year of football, he didn't want to spend it riding the bench. "Just letting them know, I understand if that's not in your vision," Burgess said. Texas State running back Torrance Burgess Jr. (4) is tackled during the game against Texas at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 5, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Burgess decided to stay. After all, he thought, who would want to pick up a running back coming off an injury? Former Texas State running back Greg Burrell's dismissal cleared Burgess' path to playing time. The Pearland native said he always knew he could be a top running back. Kinne, Nealy and Burgess' parents echoed the sentiment. None of them saw this coming, though. Burgess averages 7.8 yards per attempt and 139.6 yards per contest, both the best marks in the country. Only Missouri running back Jamal Roberts leads him in total yards, and he's played one extra game. Burgess doesn't run a 4.2 40-yard dash. His measurements on Texas State profile page are probably a generous estimate. None of that has mattered through six games. "He's just seeing the field so well. His vision, quickness and make you miss in the box," Kinne said. "I mean, we haven't had that ever since I've been here." Burgess is naturally humble. His parents said that at UTEP, he would take himself out of the game, allowing his teammates more opportunities. Nealy raves about his protégé's character, work ethic and the way he lifts those around him. Despite the success in 2026, Burgess has a chip on his shoulder the size of the Lone Star State. Whatever doubters still exist are simply fuel for his engine. "Every time something gets tough or gets hard, I look back and say, ‘Remember your why,"' Burgess said. "They don't believe it? Go make them believe." Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. This article originally published at 'Go make them believe': Texas State RB Torrance Burgess Jr. powers nation's top offense .

item.title: NEC Men’s Basketball Season Preview
item.description: The NEC knelt to the sword of The Reef last season. LIU ran through the league at 15-3. They won the conference tournament to return to the NCAA Tournament, all while fans brought their hands together above their heads on free throws. “Fins Up” became a national story . But can the Sharks go back-to-back? Le Moyne is eligible for the NCAA Tournament for the first time, but will also be leaving the conference for the Metro at the end of the year. Mercyhurst has some fun returners, and Central Connecticut is always going to be in the mix. What’s in store for the NEC this year? 1. LIU WHAT I LIKE: The talent is impossible to deny. LIU is by far the most talented group in the NEC once again. Vasean Allette was a double-digit scorer at a high-major; he’s way too good for this level. Easy pick for preseason Player of the Year. He’ll be flanked by former high-major recruits Jakhi Howard and Daquan Davis, who bring a level of athleticism and pedigree to this team that the rest of the NEC guards can’t match. item.content:encoded: The NEC knelt to the sword of The Reef last season. LIU ran through the league at 15-3. They won the conference tournament to return to the NCAA Tournament, all while fans brought their hands together above their heads on free throws. “Fins Up” became a national story . But can the Sharks go back-to-back? Le Moyne is eligible for the NCAA Tournament for the first time, but will also be leaving the conference for the Metro at the end of the year. Mercyhurst has some fun returners, and Central Connecticut is always going to be in the mix. What’s in store for the NEC this year? 1. LIU WHAT I LIKE: The talent is impossible to deny. LIU is by far the most talented group in the NEC once again. Vasean Allette was a double-digit scorer at a high-major; he’s way too good for this level. Easy pick for preseason Player of the Year. He’ll be flanked by former high-major recruits Jakhi Howard and Daquan Davis, who bring a level of athleticism and pedigree to this team that the rest of the NEC guards can’t match. The huge swing pieces are the Bewley twins – Matt and Ryan – in the frontcourt. They are former highly-ranked recruits who have been embroiled in a legal fight with the NCAA for years . The Sharks also brought in Tyrell Bowles, a highly productive JUCO big man, along with a few Division I transfers to fill out the backcourt depth. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: There’s a reason that these guys are in the NEC. Allette was dismissed from the Old Dominion team his freshman year and didn’t play last season at UTSA due to personal reasons. Howard left the Utah team in January last year after transferring in from Auburn, where he was famously involved in a brawl on a flight. The Bewley brothers have their aforementioned legal battle and haven’t suited up in a college basketball game in years. However, Rod Strickland has had success with mercurial personalities. Last year’s group was similarly combustible, but he took them to the NCAA Tournament. 2. MERCYHURST WHAT I LIKE: The only returning player in the league to make an All-Conference team last year is Mercyhurst point guard Jake Lemelman. He’s a dynamite scoring guard who improved in every aspect of his game a year ago, especially in terms of creating his own shot inside the arc. Gary Manchel went out and added American transfer Geoff Sprouse late in the cycle to help him out, while a healthy Marcus Jackson can provide some defensive punch. Daemar Kelly and Tennessee Rainwater are also proven producers in the NEC, and will give some additional scoring alongside Lemelman. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: Mercyhurst doesn’t have a lot of bodies in the frontcourt. However, if Cal State LA transfer Deraje Agbaosi can continue to produce the way he did in an exhibition against Buffalo (20 points, 11 rebounds, 4 blocks), that won’t be a huge problem. Even then, as Agbaosi is just 6-foot-7, the Lakers are thin in terms of legit size on this roster. 3. CENTRAL CONNECTICUT WHAT I LIKE: Patrick Sellers lost all five starters before last season, and still put together a top-2 finish in NEC play. The Blue Devils have the best coach in the conference, which will give them a chance on any given night. Especially in the NEC, where portal and JUCO evaluations are so important, and finding the right fit matters, having an elite coach is such an upper hand. Raphel Laurent should be a star scorer coming in from UMass Boston, where he averaged 22.4 points per game as a sophomore last season on 60 TS%. Perhaps a breakout season could be in order for James Jones with a little more than just being the fifth starter. Brayden Jackson redshirted at St. Bonaventure last season, and brings some punch in the frontcourt. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: The last few CCSU teams have at least held a pipeline of returning talent to believe in. Sure, they lost all five starters from 2025, but Jay Rodgers was coming back healthy, Darin Smith’s breakout could be seen a mile away, and Max Frazier had some impressive moments as a sophomore in 2025. Can Daniel James replicate Frazier’s breakout? It’s a little fuzzier to try to see the stars aligning for the Blue Devils now than it was an offseason ago. 4. LE MOYNE WHAT I LIKE: There’s some serious depth in the Le Moyne backcourt. Even if Ametri Moss isn’t eligible, the Dolphins can play Sac State transfer Jayden Teat, UT Martin transfer Damien King, Bryant transfer sharpshooter Khalil Williams, Swiss freshman Leo Gysel, JUCO transfer Kole Williams, and NJIT transfer Jeremy Clayville. All of those guys will have a role for Le Moyne. As will Northeastern transfer Ty Francis, an athletic four-man. Nate Champion’s team will shoot a ton of threes and have plenty of guards that can create those threes. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: The Dolphins have had an All-Conference forward or big each of the last three seasons in the NEC, but this season, it’s less likely. VMI transfer Kaden Stuckey has to be a big-time rebounder for Le Moyne, and backup big man Przemek Hartman needs to be ready to contribute off the bench. How many minutes can Le Moyne survive with Francis or Trevor Roe at the five if they can’t get consistent big man production. 5. WAGNER WHAT I LIKE: Aside from LIU, this is the most athletic team in the NEC. Youssof Singare was a backup big man for UConn, and then for High Point, but the athletic 6-foot-11 shot blocker should be a defensive monster in the NEC. Add in Tajae Jones, a Siena transfer known for his athleticism, along with Kareem Watson and Baron Smith, and Wagner has a deep frontcourt of options. Heck, even former Syracuse and New Orleans 7-footer William Patterson is an interesting upside swing. If the Seahawks can get Fairfield transfer Cam Estevez playing at his best, then he’s an All-NEC scoring guard. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: Even though the makeup of the frontcourt is fun, there’s essentially nothing proven. None of the five have ever played more than 25% of the minutes in a Division I season. Point guard is a question mark for me as well. Fordham transfer Ryan Pettis is more combo than point, and Taj Bryant struggled at Sacred Heart. This team could be brutal offensively, but Wagner has won with poor offense before. 6. FDU WHAT I LIKE: Pepperdine transfer Pavle Stosic has the chance to be one of the better big men in the conference. He’s a physical bruiser at 6-foot-10, 230 pounds with rebounding ability. He’ll pair with Bol Agu to make a super burly frontcourt for the Knights, something that the program has generally lacked. Division II transfer point guard JR Jacobs can be electric. He can be the next sub-6-foot PG to make an impact for the Knights, following in the footsteps of Grant Singleton, Demetre Roberts, and Bullet Jamison. JUCO transfer Vophcy Prophete will provide some scoring as well. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: While Stosic and Agu are physical, they don’t have a ton of proven scoring chops. They’ll probably be reliant on getting efficient scoring out of the guards, unless they can overwhelm on the offensive glass to a point where it doesn’t matter. Perhaps we see a leap from the returning David Jevtic or Raysean Johnson. Austin Peay transfer Travis Torain can also be a big swing piece. 7. STONEHILL WHAT I LIKE: Stonehill’s offseason was predicated on adding players who won. The Skyhawks are betting on former Yale guard Devon Arlington to take a step forward at the point, and with the drop in levels, I can buy in on a breakout year. Former Navy wing Jack Medaille had a strong campaign at Division II Saint Anselm, a 25-win team. Idaho transfer Ewan Steele should also be a valuable frontcourt piece. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: Outside of Medaille, there’s not a lot of guys who have proven college production on this roster. Arlington’s numbers were brutal for the Bulldogs. They’ll be reliant on a leap from injury returner Will Batchelder. In the frontcourt, Steele needs to take a leap on both sides of the ball. item.title: Texas Southern vs. Southern: How to watch, date, time, TV channel
item.description: Texas Southern looks to rebound from consecutive tough losses in SWAC play when it faces Southern at Reliant Stadium. (Andrew Richardson) It's a home game, but at a much larger venue for Texas Southern this week. The Tigers (1-5, 0-3 SWAC) host Southern (3-4, 1-2) on Saturday afternoon at Reliant Stadium looking to end a five-game losing streak. TSU's past two conference losses have been gut punches. Last week, the Tigers gave up 24 fourth-quarter points and were unable to hold a 10-point lead with roughly five minutes left in a loss to Mississippi Valley State. Two weeks earlier, TSU overcame a 22-point deficit in the second half only to lose in overtime at Alcorn State. Southern, coached by Pro Football Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk, was off last week after winning at Prairie View A&M. The Jaguars lead the all-time series 14-4, but TSU has won two of the past three meetings. Texas Southern vs. Southern When: 2 p.m. Saturday Where: Reliant Stadium TV: SWAC TV Radio: 90.9 FM with Devan Wade and Lary Hale 2026 Texas Southern football schedule Aug. 29: Beat North Carolina Central, 42-30 Sept. 6: lost to Prairie View A&M, 52-14 Sept. 12: lost to UTEP, 51-10 Sept. 26: lost to Alcorn State, 43-40 (OT) Oct. 3: lost to Florida Atlantic, 66-10 Oct. 10: lost to Mississippi Valley State, 38-34 Oct. 24: vs. Southern at Reliant Stadium, 2 p.m. (SWAC TV) Oct. 31: vs. Grambling State at Thorne Stadium, 7:30 p.m. (SWAC TV) Nov. 7: vs. Alabama State at Thorne Stadium, 2 p.m. (SWAC TV) Nov. 14: at Alabama A&M, 2 p.m. (SWAC TV) Nov. 21: vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff at Thorne Stadium, 2 p.m. (SWAC TV) Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: Dodgers Urged To Trade Shohei Ohtani After Injury Setback
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 15: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts after striking out against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game four of the National League Championship Series at Dodger Stadium on October 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty Images The Los Angeles Dodgers entered the season hoping to make history with a third consecutive World Series championship. Instead, their pursuit ended with a sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, raising questions about how the organization can get more out of its aging and expensive roster next season. And some of those questions have surrounded two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani. The four-time MVP endured an injury-disrupted second half that affected his production at the plate and ultimately prevented him from pitching in the postseason. With the Dodgers preparing for another championship push, his two-way responsibilities have become a subject of renewed scrutiny. But the team has declared that he will continue to pitch as well as hit into the future, despite the injury setbacks. “Ohtani was attempting his first full-time two-way season in three years, and doing so at age 32 proved more difficult than at 29,” Alden Gonzalez noted for ESPN. “(Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew) Friedman acknowledged that Ohtani’s offensive struggles ‘certainly had an impact’ on the Dodgers’ early exit.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cardinals’ 5-Year Veteran Draws Interest From Astros Los Angeles Dodgers Urged To Trade Shohei Ohtani If He Won’t Stop Pitching Ohtani’s difficulties have prompted some observers to question whether the benefits of using him as both a hitter and pitcher still outweigh the physical demands. One particularly forceful argument calls for Los Angeles to end his pitching career altogether, or trade him away if he won’t accept that change. “They need to pull him off the pitching mound permanently. And if he insists on continuing this detrimental charade, they need to seriously consider trading him,” longtime Los Angeles Times columnist Bill Plaschke urged . “Shohei Ohtani as a two-way player has become a one-way ticket to disaster, and if he’s not willing to accept that reality, maybe he should be offered a one-way ticket out of Los Angeles.” While attempting to trade the most popular and talented player in the sport might seem drastic, Plaschke emphasized the physical toll of Ohtani’s two-way workload. “His body is changing,” he added. ‘His skills are changing. He’s 32, with 13 seasons of professional baseball burdening his lumbering 6-foot-4 frame, and part of his game is slowly disintegrating under the weight. The problem is his pitching. It’s hurting him. It’s distracting him. It’s exhausting him.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cubs Castoff Wins World Series Championship With Brewers Or Rays Los Angeles Dodgers Face Shohei Ohtani Trade Call After Injury Derails Three-Pe

One particularly forceful argument calls for Los Angeles to end his pitching career altogether, or trade him away if he won’t accept that change. “They need to pull him off the pitching mound permanently. And if he insists on continuing this detrimental charade, they need to seriously consider trading him,” longtime Los Angeles Times columnist Bill Plaschke urged . “Shohei Ohtani as a two-way player has become a one-way ticket to disaster, and if he’s not willing to accept that reality, maybe he should be offered a one-way ticket out of Los Angeles.” While attempting to trade the most popular and talented player in the sport might seem drastic, Plaschke emphasized the physical toll of Ohtani’s two-way workload. “His body is changing,” he added. ‘His skills are changing. He’s 32, with 13 seasons of professional baseball burdening his lumbering 6-foot-4 frame, and part of his game is slowly disintegrating under the weight. The problem is his pitching. It’s hurting him. It’s distracting him. It’s exhausting him.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cubs Castoff Wins World Series Championship With Brewers Or Rays Los Angeles Dodgers Face Shohei Ohtani Trade Call After Injury Derails Three-Peat Shortly after the team’s season ended, Friedman noted surgery was not being considered for Ohtani’s knee or biceps issues and that he expected the superstar to pitch again next season, emphasizing the value of the two-way production. Ohtani finished the season with an 8-2 pitching record and a 1.79 ERA across 85⅔ innings, while batting .275 with 30 home runs in 135 games, though he seemed to run out of gas when the Dodgers needed him most this month. The challenge is finding a way to keep him healthy and productive through an entire season, particularly when the organization’s ultimate goal is another championship. After injuries disrupted his 2026 campaign and the club fell short of a historic three-peat, figuring out how to manage his workload will be among their most consequential offseason decisions. Despite the prominent chatter, though, a trade is virtually unthinkable. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: ‘Is that Eddie Lacy?’ – NFL fans have noticed a big Josh Jacobs change after his Packers return
item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have been able to welcome back running back Josh Jacobs to practice ahead of their game this weekend against the Detroit Lions. To say the Packers’ running game has been struggling without him would be the understatement of the century. There is no team in the entire NFL with fewer rushing yards per game (59.8) than the Packers. Jacobs’ return will still divide fans across the league but it will be very much welcomed by those in Green Bay given their struggles. The running back again apologised profusely for his actions during the offseason, speaking earlier in the week from the Packers’ locker room. Although his return will be viewed as a major boost by the Packers, some fans have shared their concerns over Jacobs’ fitness ahead of Sunday’s trip to Detroit. NFL fans notice something different about Josh Jacobs upon Packers return Having only just been removed from the commissioner’s exempt list, Jacobs is in line to make his first appearance of the season for the Packers. However, to what extent he will be able to play remains a mystery as some fans feel he has returned slightly overweight. ‘On that Eddie Lacy diet,’ replied one fan on X. ‘Pulled up like prime Eddie,’ added another. Jacobs scored 13 touchdowns and racked up just shy of 1,000 rushing yards (929) last season for the Packers. His return will mark a significant boost if he is able to show this level of form when he takes to the field. ‘”Look at me, look at me, I’m the fullback now”,’ another fan jokingly replied. ‘Looking like prime Eddie Lacy,’ yet another fan said on X. Former Packers running back Eddie Lacy was criticised by Mike McCarthy during his time in Green Bay over his weight. When he joined the Seattle Seahawks, weight targets were included in his contract as incentives to maintain his fitness. ‘Is that Eddie Lacy?’ responded another fan. ‘Not trying to troll at all but Eddie Lacy?,’ said another. Read more: ‘Very disappointing outcome’- Fans voice frustration as Patriots fall 30-24 to Bears ‘Very easy explanation’ – Tom Brady speaks on the Patriots overtaking the Bills in his power rankings ‘Never seen this happen’ – Ben Roethlisberger has spotted ‘unusual’ Aaron Rodgers issue

item.title: Browns Give Blunt Reason for Backing Watson Over Shedeur Sanders
item.description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders will remain in the backup role. Getty EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 11: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns in action during the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 11: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns is tackled by David Bailey #31 of the New York Jets during the first quarter of the game at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty Todd Monken’s decision to start Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders came down to what he saw when the veteran quarterback was at his best. On The Pivot, the Cleveland Browns coach revisited the competition and offered a candid explanation of what separated the two quarterbacks in his staff’s eyes. “It wasn’t like Shedeur didn’t have his fair share of great plays, but we just saw a little bit more from Deshaun at the top end,” Monken said. “I think what we saw as a collective staff was his best. I think you try to look at what a player’s best is and then try to minimize the weaknesses. I think that’s with every player. I think that’s what we saw with Deshaun.” Monken named Watson the starter on August 24, following an evaluation that included the offseason program, training camp, a joint practice with Buffalo and two preseason games. At the time, he acknowledged the decision had not come easily. Todd Monken Points to Change in Deshaun Watson’s Reception Getty EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – OCTOBER 11: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns in action during the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 11, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) The decision to go with Watson did not come without some blowback . But Monken pointed to the Browns’ Week 4 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers as a moment that showed how quickly Watson’s reception in Cleveland could change. “So here we go from being booed, to they don’t want him as the starter, to we’re playing the Steelers, and we introduce him last coming out of the tunnel, and they cheer the heck out of him,” Monken said. “And that just goes to tell you what our fans really want. They want good football. They want our players to play well. They want something to cheer about, something that gives them optimism.” Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 that night thanks to a late go-ahead drive, giving Monken and Watson a division win on a national stage. The next step is making that level of offensive play more dependable. The Browns have continued finding ways to win, but their latest victory required another late escape after an unproductive first half. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) The Browns improved to 4-2 and moved into first place in the AFC North with their 13-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens . Cleveland managed just 46 net yards before halftime and punted on all five first-half possessions. Watson delivered when the Browns needed him late. His 33-yard completion to Jerry Jeudy helped set up Andre Szmyt’s winning field goal, capping a 10-play, 62-yard possession. It marked Cleveland’s fourth late go-ahead drive of the season. But he’s just got something in him, the ability to make a play when needed,” Monken said. “We just kind of flatten out some of the other ups and downs that we have. And it starts with me, starts with our offensive staff. And that’s going to always be the case. It’s a we thing, not an individual thing.” Monken offered a similar acknowledgment during The Pivot interview. “It’s a work in progress,” he said. “We’re always under construction.” The Browns’ next opportunity to put together a more complete offensive performance comes Sunday when they travel to face the 1-5 Tennessee Titans . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There are ordinary sports Fridays, and then there is what Milwaukee is about to experience on October 23. The city has an NBA home opener on the schedule, its first World Series game in 44 years coming later that evening and a sports community preparing for a celebration that could last well into the night. The Milwaukee Bucks have decided that the occasion is so special that they are changing their own schedule to accommodate it. Instead of hosting the Chicago Bulls at 7 p.m. CT, the Bucks will begin their home opener at 3 p.m., allowing fans to turn their attention to the Brewers' World Series opener against Tampa Bay at 7 p.m. It is not every day that an NBA franchise adjusts its schedule because the baseball team across town has accomplished something extraordinary. But the Brewers' return to the Fall Classic has created exactly that situation. The Bucks made an unusual decision The Bucks announced the schedule change after Milwaukee completed its sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. With the Brewers preparing to host their first World Series game since 1982, the NBA team recognized that a normal evening tipoff would create a significant conflict for local fans. Clock out. Tip off. Cheer on! 🏀 Bucks home opener at 3 p.m. ⚾️ Watch party in Deer District at 7 p.m. — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) October 22, 2026 Working with the NBA, Milwaukee moved its game against Chicago four hours earlier. The change gives basketball fans a chance to watch the Bucks before turning their attention to one of the most anticipated baseball games in franchise history. For ambitious fans attending both games, the arrangement creates an unusual doubleheader. Fiserv Forum and American Family Field are both located in Milwaukee, meaning someone could potentially attend an NBA game in the afternoon and a World Series game that evening. Tip off. Cheer on! 🏀 Bucks home opener at 3 p.m. ⚾️ Watch party in Deer District at 7 p.m. — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) October 22, 2026 Working with the NBA, Milwaukee moved its game against Chicago four hours earlier. The change gives basketball fans a chance to watch the Bucks before turning their attention to one of the most anticipated baseball games in franchise history. For ambitious fans attending both games, the arrangement creates an unusual doubleheader. Fiserv Forum and American Family Field are both located in Milwaukee, meaning someone could potentially attend an NBA game in the afternoon and a World Series game that evening. Tickets, travel logistics and the timing of the basketball game's conclusion would still need to cooperate. Nevertheless, the possibility alone illustrates how extraordinary Friday could become for Milwaukee sports fans. The Brewers are chasing something the Bucks already experienced The Bucks know what a championship can mean to Milwaukee. Their 2021 NBA title, led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, ended a 50-year championship drought and produced an enormous celebration throughout the city. The Brewers are chasing an achievement they have never experienced. Milwaukee reached the World Series in 1982 but lost to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games. The franchise has spent the following decades trying to return, often competing against teams with significantly larger financial resources. Now the Brewers have another opportunity, and their opponent makes the matchup even more fascinating. Tampa Bay has also never won a World Series, guaranteeing that one franchise will celebrate its first championship when the series concludes. That creates an atmosphere considerably different from a championship series featuring perennial contenders. For Milwaukee fans, every game carries the possibility of something their city has never witnessed. MORE : Shai Gilgeous-Alexander made an unusual choice as his 141-game streak ended Milwaukee could have a sports day fans remember forever The Bucks' decision is about more than television ratings or competing events. It reflects the unusual relationship between professional sports franchises and the communities they represent. When one team reaches a historic moment, the celebration can extend well beyond that particular sport. Milwaukee's sports calendar has suddenly become a shared occasion. Basketball fans have their home opener, baseball fans have the World Series, and those who follow both teams have a Friday that might require clearing their entire schedule. There is also a wonderful contrast between the two franchises. The Bucks have recently reached the summit of professional basketball, while the Brewers are still searching for their first baseball championship. Both organizations will have an opportunity to celebrate with their supporters on the same day. The Bucks will still want to beat Chicago, and the Brewers will still need to handle a dangerous Tampa Bay team. Neither outcome is guaranteed. But the schedule itself has already become part of the story. Milwaukee does not need to choose between basketball and baseball on Friday. Thanks to an unusual decision by the Bucks, the city has a chance to enjoy both. item.description: ⚽ All the latest news going into the weekend’s action ⚽ Premier League: weekend guide | Mail Tom Álvaro Arbeloa’s been talking ahead of Fulham’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, and buoyed up by last weekend’s much needed win over Hull. “Nothing has changed for us,” insisted the manager, “we were not winning games but we believed in ourselves, we were doing so many things well, “The most important thing [about the Hull win] is we were in same situation against Manchester United and Ipswich but didn’t win but now we had to improve in our transition and did. We controlled the ball in their half better than before.” As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Sunday’s match at Camp Nou will be watched by hundreds of millions of viewers all over the world. A clásico always carries significance, but this weekend’s edition will be especially significant. A Barça win would move them nine points clear of their rivals at the top of La Liga . A Real Madrid victory could be a catalyst for the rest of their season. Continue reading...

item.title: Mika Baur delivers brutal Celtic verdict after Celta Vigo Europa League defeat
item.description: Mika Baur delivers brutal Celtic verdict after Celta Vigo Europa League defeat Celtic midfielder Mika Baur has delivered a damning assessment of his side’s second-half collapse against Celta Vigo. The German opened the scoring at Celtic Park, but a quickfire double from Javi Rodriguez turned the contest on its head and condemned Martin O’Neill’s side to another European defeat. Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Baur made no attempt to disguise his frustration with Celtic’s inability to build on their advantage. He said: “Very disappointed in the end. We scored, I thought we had a good ten minutes, and then we were too passive. “They dominated us in our own half, around our own box. We had no control with the ball, we defended not well enough… so yeah. I think how we played the second half, or the last 30 minutes, it’s deserved in the end.” Asked why Celtic had surrendered control of the contest, Baur offered a brutally honest response. “I cannot tell you. I’m sorry. I have no idea.” The midfielder was also critical of his side’s failure to retain possession and halt Celta’s momentum after conceding. “Absolutely. It can happen when you get a goal. They can score as well, good team. “So then, you should get the control back. Hold the ball a bit longer to take the momentum away from them, maybe. Like us at the moment, after our goal, it’s always like that. So you should break that, but we did not.” Despite Celtic’s precarious position in the Europa League, Baur insisted the players have not given up hope of reaching the knockout stages. “What else should we do? Yeah, absolutely. There’s still games ahead, so we go with all our best to qualify for the next round. “It’s not getting easier with a loss again, so yeah. We need points.” HAVE YOUR SAY – Join the Celtic conversation in our comments section below… Celtic in the Fifties by Matt Corr, in two volumes, both published on 4th September 2026 by Celtic Star Books. item.title: Getafe president responds after José Bordalás launches furious attack on club
item.description: Getafe president responds after José Bordalás launches furious attack on club Getafe president Ángel Torres has responded to José Bordalás after the manager accused the club of failing to fulfil its promises following Thursday’s 5-2 home defeat by Lugano in the Conference League . Bordalás criticised the quality of his squad and admitted he felt “deceived” by the club’s board. “We do not have the ability to compete in three competitions, or even one,” he said, adding that he was angry with the performance and the promises he believes have not been kept. “I love Getafe and this is very painful,” the manager added. Torres: “The door is open” Speaking to Cadena SER on Friday, Torres strongly rejected the suggestion that he had betrayed the manager. “To say I betrayed him... You need a face of concrete to say that to me after 30 years, when I have never betrayed him, or anyone else,” the president said. Torres also made it clear that Bordalás could leave if he was unhappy at the club. “He signed because he wanted to, but if we are so bad, the door is open,” he said, insisting that Getafe have one of the best squads in the club’s history. Getafe, currently 15th in La Liga , now turn their attention to this weekend’s trip to face Athletic Bilbao . Despite the public disagreement, Torres has made his expectations clear ahead of the match. “To win, simple as that,” he said.

item.title: UFC 333 fight will go ahead despite 4.5 pound weight miss
item.description: ABU DHABI, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES - OCTOBER 23: Nicolle Caliari of Brazil poses on the scale during the UFC 333 official weigh-ins at Hilton Abu Dhabi Yas Island on October 23, 2026 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Iasmin Lucindo will still fight Nicolle Caliari in the first fight of the night at UFC 333, despite Caliari missing weight by a whopping 4.5 pounds. Caliari stepped on the scales in Abu Dhabi at 120.5 pounds, which isn’t even close to the 116 pound limit for women’s strawweight. Lucindo (and the other 17 fighters on the card) made weight without a problem. See the full UFC 333 weigh-in results here. While a weight miss that big could result in a fight cancellation, the bout will go ahead as a catchweight and Caliari will forfeit 30% of her purse to Lucindo. We’re not too surprised that Lucindo agreed to go ahead with the fight. She’s coming off a nine month suspension due to a drug test failure for mesterolone, with Combat Sports Anti-Doping (CSAD) determining the cause was consistent with unintentional contamination of supplements. She didn’t sit out for nearly a year and then fly all the way from Brazil to Abu Dhabi not to compete. Lucindo is 18-6 in MMA and 5-2 with UFC with her sole loss in six fights a decision loss to Amanda Lemos back in 2025. Caliari is 9-4 in MMA and 1-2 in UFC with her sole victory being a submission win over Shauna Bannon back in May. This is her first recorded incident of missed weight. UFC 333 goes down from Abu Dhabi this Saturday October 23rd with the early prelims kicking off at 10 a.m. EST / 7 a.m. PT. So you’ll have to tune in early if you want to see how Lucindo vs. Caliari goes following this big weight miss.

item.title: Emery's Villa 2.0 reboot restores optimism before Man City meeting
item.description: Aston Villa fans were in buoyant mood before the Champions League win against Viking at Villa Park [Getty Images] When Aston Villa walked out to face Viking in the Champions League, a giant tifo emblazoned with the message 'We've Conquered Before. We're Prepared For More' dropped down from Villa Park's famous Holte End. At the same time, Villa manager Unai Emery was striding along the touchline to a standing ovation as he took the acclaim from supporters. Emery celebrates the fourth anniversary of his appointment from Villarreal when Villa face Premier League leaders Manchester City at Villa Park on Saturday lunchtime, his arrival a transformative moment for one of the great old footballing institutions. He has written his name into Villa Park history, adding to a track record there and at other clubs that marks him down as one of the game's elite operators. And it was reflected in every moment against Viking with an emphatic victory. Villa Park's mood was buoyant and expectant - restored to the state of optimism that came with last season's Europa League triumph following a campaign that saw 54-year-old Emery return the club to the Champions League. It was in sharp contrast to some trepidation weeks earlier after a summer which saw a host of big names depart and Villa deliver what has become something of a trademark under Emery, a slow start that usually ends with the closure of the transfer window. The scale of change at Villa can be underscored by the fact six of the starting line-up that won the Europa League with a 3-0 win against Freiburg in Istanbul in May left during the summer. Norwegians Viking were duly dispatched 3-1 amid more jubilation, Villa making it three wins from three and actually topping the standings in the Champions League table until Peter Christiansen's late goal for the visitors left them level on nine points with holders Paris St-Germain, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis. It followed on from the 6-0 win against Fenerbahce in the Champions League at Villa Park. Villa have now won 12 European home games in a row, under the great specialist Emery. Little wonder, then, that Emery was elated as he looked ahead to Saturday's meeting with Manchester City, who have a 100% record from seven games. Villa Park is certain to be high on excitement and emotion as Emery said: "Those three points fills us with confidence. We are comfortable, and of course as well getting balance, because after this match we are going to play against Barcelona, favourites, and then we play against Galatasaray away." He also noted how Villa Park is right on board with his impressive transition into what can be described as "Villa 2.0", saying: "We now try to focus now on the Manchester City game on Saturday, hopefully the same atmosphere, the same energy. I am so, so happy but we must keep moving forward with the challenges we are going to face. "There's still a lot of work to do, so how we are responding, getting better, is really fantastic." Aston

Little wonder, then, that Emery was elated as he looked ahead to Saturday's meeting with Manchester City, who have a 100% record from seven games. Villa Park is certain to be high on excitement and emotion as Emery said: "Those three points fills us with confidence. We are comfortable, and of course as well getting balance, because after this match we are going to play against Barcelona, favourites, and then we play against Galatasaray away." He also noted how Villa Park is right on board with his impressive transition into what can be described as "Villa 2.0", saying: "We now try to focus now on the Manchester City game on Saturday, hopefully the same atmosphere, the same energy. I am so, so happy but we must keep moving forward with the challenges we are going to face. "There's still a lot of work to do, so how we are responding, getting better, is really fantastic." Aston Villa manager Unai Emery - here celebrating a goal against Viking - has looked even more energised than usual in recent times [Getty Images] Emery, if it is possible, appeared even more animated than usual during the Viking game, looking energised by the renewal he had to perform in the summer and the promise shown by Villa's new players. The list of summer departures looked daunting, with keeper Emiliano Martinez, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans leaving, along with England trio Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Morgan Rogers - the latter duo to Arsenal and Chelsea for a combined total of £172m as Villa raked in about £320m. They had been integral to that Europa League win, the club's first European trophy for 44 years when they won the European Cup, and first domestic triumph since the League Cup win in 1996. Villa's start to the season was slow, losing 4-0 at Brighton - with all four goals scored before half-time - then 1-0 at home to Arsenal. A goalless draw at Hull City was followed by 2-1 loss to Nottingham Forest at Villa Park. The duck was broken with their first win at Spurs. Suddenly Villa and Emery looked like their old selves, culminating in those victories against Fenerbahce, a fine 1-0 win at Newcastle United, and Viking. And what will please Emery and Villa's fans - who never wavered in their total faith in the manager they worship - is how the new signings have been contributing, suggesting the magician has produced a winning formula again, and quickly. It will come as no surprise given Emery's back catalogue of work, which includes three successive Europa League wins with Sevilla, another with Villarreal and of course Villa's triumph. Even in what is regarded as an unrewarding spell at Arsenal, he still took them to the final of competition in 2019, although they lost to Chelsea. It is why Villa's hierarchy, led by co-owner, Nassef Sawiris, give Emery everything he requires where possible. Alongside sales, Villa spent £280m, and the early signs are they have invested wisely. Unai Emery has lost six of the players that started the Europa League final win against Freiburg in May, including goalkeeper Emi Martinez [Getty Images] Against Viking, 20-year-old Brazilian Alysson, playing on the right flank, was Villa's most impressive performer. He preceded the summer signings, arriving from Gremio in January in a deal that could eventually be worth £10.4m. He terrorised Viking with his pace, and even if his finishing still appears raw, he looks a superb prospect. Alysson won a penalty for Emiliano Buendia to put Villa two up, then ended a surging run by seeing his cross deflected into his own net by Henrik Heggheim for the third. Ibrahim Mbaye, an 18-year-old signed in a £47m deal from Paris Saint-Germain, also showed flashed of rich promise on the other wing, a tantalising future partnership for Villa fans. He appeared in all four of Senegal's matches at the 2026 World Cup, netting in a 3-1 defeat by France to become the youngest African player to score at a men's World Cup. New keeper Zion Suzuki, the 24-year-old Japan keeper brought in from Parma for £30m, had big gloves to fill in replacing cult hero Martinez, but has looked assured, with the added bonus of an outstanding range of short and long passing that gives Villa an added dimension. Joao Gomes, the midfielder in at £38m from Wolverhampton Wanderers, also showed what he offers against Viking. Emery turned to a player who knew well to replace Watkins after he left to join Al-Hilal in the Saudi Pro League, signing Nicolas Jackson, who he coached at Villarreal, for £65m from Chelsea. He has settled quickly with five goals already. Johan Manzambi, seen here celebrating his winner at Newcastle United, is one of a crop of exciting new Aston Villa signings [Getty Images] Arguably the most exciting arrival of all is Johan Manzambi, a break-out World Cup star with Switzerland. The 21-year-old midfielder cost a little more than £50m from Freiburg. It was a deal pulled out from under the noses of Newcastle United, leaving then manager Eddie Howe devastated. He piled on the agony with the winner at St James' Park after scoring on his full debut in the victory at Spurs, although he is currently a doubt to face Manchester City. Emery has not just made it a case of out with the old and in with the new as he rebuilds Villa. Captain John McGinn remains the heartbeat of his side, while former England midfielder Ross Barkley is undergoing a late career renaissance. The 32-year-old scored against Viking, his fourth this season, also scoring twice in the rout against Fenerbahce. Barkley was a surprise signing from Luton Town in July 2024, having had a season on loan at Villa Park in the 2020-21 season. Emery is a huge admirer and said after the win against Viking: "As a person, he is a fantastic guy. Ross Barkley is a very good player with experience, and his career, I don't know why, was going down after Chelsea. "When we wa

item.title: U.S. To Host First-Ever Women’s Soccer Club World Cup
item.description: Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost . The United States will host the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced on Thursday. The tournament, to be held every four years, will feature 19 of the best women’s club soccer teams from all six confederations (AFC, CAF, Concacaf, CONMEBOL, OFC and UEFA). The competition will run from Jan. 5-30, 2028, with the host cities yet to be determined. Previous reports said Los Angeles and San Diego were being considered, per ESPN. FIFA chief women’s football officer Sarai Bareman said the U.S. was selected based on the recent success of the 2025 Men’s Club World Cup and 2026 World Cup. “We undertook a detailed assessment to identify the most suitable host for the inaugural edition of the FIFA Women’s Club World Cup,” Bareman said. “Ultimately, the United States’ recent excellence in staging top FIFA tournaments, combined with the significant interest in women’s football there plus its elite sporting infrastructure, made the country the standout option.” Also in the news: The Family Of A 1-Year-Old Mississippi Boy Says Video Shows His Killing By Police Was Not Justified Seven teams have already qualified for the 2028 Women’s Club World Cup: Arsenal (England), Club America (Mexico), Barcelona ( Spain ), Gotham FC (United States), Naegohyang Women’s FC (North Korea), SC Corinthians (Brazil) and Wuhan Jiangda WFC (China). “These seven clubs, and a dozen more, will come together to show the strength and depth of women’s club football to a global audience,” Bareman said. “They will have the opportunity to tell their story, expand their fan base and represent their club on the world stage. They have thoroughly earned this opportunity to be part of history in the United States.” The AFC, CAF, Concacaf and CONMEBOL will each of three teams in the field, while the OFC will have one and UEFA will have six. Also on Thursday, FIFA’s Bureau of Council approved the distribution of $2.5 million in preparation money to each participating member association for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. That is the same amount FIFA distributed for the men’s World Cup played this summer in North America, and an increase from $960,000 ahead of the 2023 Women’s World Cup. Fantasy Takeaway: Godwin becomes a high-volume flex or WR2 option if Egbuka sits and Godwin practices without limitations. Gainwell's 17 targets confirms he's already holding a primary role in Tampa Bay's passing game . An increase in third-down participation could boost Gainwell's PPR floor. Chris Godwin (Highest Floor & Ceiling) The primary beneficiary. If healthy, Godwin should command the largest portion of Egbuka's vacated 26% target share. 2. Ted Hurts III (Speculative Sleeper): High-upside play for deeper leagues or flex spots if you need home-run potential. 3. Kenneth Gainwell (Floor Boost Only): A modest bump that raises his floor slightly in deep leagues. item.title: Former Man United chief Murtough joins Birmingham
item.description: John Murtough was Manchester United football director from March 2021 to April 2024 [Birmingham City FC] Birmingham City have appointed former Manchester United chief John Murtough as their new director of football. Murtough, 55, who left United in April 2024 as football director after 11 years at Old Trafford, becomes the replacement for Craig Gardner, who departed St Andrew's in June. Murtough, who has also worked for Everton, Fulham and Coventry City, was with the Premier League before joining Manchester United in 2013. His most recent role was in Serie A as director of global development at Atalanta. Murtough will begin his role at US-owned Birmingham on Monday - following this weekend's Championship game at Cardiff City. Blues currently sit fourth in the Championship after a run of three straight wins since the international break under Chris Davies. More to follow.

On the other is Nick Martinez, a 36-year-old veteran who was not necessarily the pitcher fans expected Tampa Bay to hand the ball to for the biggest game of its season. The contrast is almost too good for a Hollywood script. One pitcher can throw harder than practically anyone in baseball, while the other has built a career around experience, adjustments and finding different ways to get hitters out. Rasmussen had already handled Game 1 assignments earlier in the postseason and was available on regular rest. Instead, Tampa Bay decided to give him another day before his next appearance. The 2026 World Series is set. Who is your pick to win? https://t.co/EomSif6uww — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) October 20, 2026 That decision created an opportunity for Martinez, who posted a 15-6 record and 3.10 ERA over 180 innings during the regular season. The veteran also earned his first All-Star selection, a remarkable achievement for a pitcher who has spent years moving through different roles and organizations. Martinez has already rewarded Tampa Bay's confidence this postseason. In Game 4 of the American League Championship Series against Cleveland, he allowed one run on two hits over 5 1/3 innings. The Rays will be hoping that same combination of composure and command can help neutralize Milwaukee's offense. There is another interesting detail about the veteran. Martinez has made a habit of organizing team dinners during road trips, helping build relationships away from the ballpark. His teammates have nicknamed him "El Presidente," an appropriate title for someone who has become an important clubhouse presence. Milwaukee's young star has a completely different weapon Misiorowski does not need much introduction to anyone who has watched him pitch this season. The right-hander led Major League Baseball with a 1.80 ERA, 252 strikeouts and a 0.80 WHIP. Opponents hit just .157 against him during the regular season. His velocity is even more astonishing. During the National League Division Series against San Diego, Misiorowski threw a 104.8-mph pitch, the fastest recorded postseason offering of the pitch-tracking era. That kind of power gives Milwaukee an obvious advantage when its young starter is locating his pitches. However, there is a potential weakness Tampa Bay can exploit. The Padres and Dodgers both forced Misiorowski into elevated pitch counts during his first two postseason starts, repeatedly fouling off pitches and extending at-bats. The Brewers' ace was effective at limiting damage but did not work deep into either game. That creates an intriguing tactical battle. Tampa Bay might not need to hit Misiorowski particularly hard if it can make him throw enough pitches to reach Milwaukee's bullpen earlier than planned. MORE : Freddy Peralta's World Series opponent makes Rays ALCS MVP story even better A World Series matchup nobody would have predicted There is something refreshing about a Fall Classic featuring two franchises still chasing their first championship. The Brewers last appeared in the World Series in 1982, while Tampa Bay previously reached baseball's biggest stage in 2008 and 2020. Friday's matchup is also a reminder that baseball does not always reward the biggest names or most expensive rosters. Milwaukee and Tampa Bay have constructed winning teams through pitching development, smart roster decisions and complementary styles of play. Martinez and Misiorowski represent two completely different routes to the same opportunity. One is a veteran who has spent years earning his place. The other is a young pitcher with the kind of arm that makes radar guns look broken. Only one can win Game 1, but both have already made this World Series opener considerably more interesting than an ordinary pitching matchup. item.title: Allegri: ‘Napoli must improve out of possession and in terms of results’
item.description: Allegri: ‘Napoli must improve out of possession and in terms of results’ Massimiliano Allegri believes that the ‘most important’ thing for Napoli to do heading into their Serie A match against Roma is to improve on their work out of possession, but admits that his players need to start delivering results on a more consistent basis as well: ‘We make our judgements on results.” Napoli will host Roma at the Stadio Maradona in Serie A at 17.00 BST on Saturday evening. Allegri and his players are coming in off the back of a 4-3 Champions League victory over Bodo/Glimt , but are looking to improve on their league position after picking up 10 points from their first seven matches of the 2026-27 season. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Here is what Allegri had to say about his team’s recent results and their prospects against Roma during his pre-match press conference on Friday. Allegri’s pre-match press conference ahead of Napoli vs. Roma The first question that came Allegri’s way related to Kevin De Bruyne and his continued use in a deep midfield role. The Belgian has made it clear that he prefers to play further up the pitch where he is able to have more of an impact on attacking moves. VENICE, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli misses the penalty during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on October 17, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) When asked if he plans on using De Bruyne in the same position again, Allegri said: “These players have qualities and characteristics, he can play in front of the defence or in a double-pivot, I think he did that against Frosinone. Allegri and his players are coming in off the back of a 4-3 Champions League victory over Bodo/Glimt , but are looking to improve on their league position after picking up 10 points from their first seven matches of the 2026-27 season. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammate Kevin De Bruyne during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Here is what Allegri had to say about his team’s recent results and their prospects against Roma during his pre-match press conference on Friday. Allegri’s pre-match press conference ahead of Napoli vs. Roma The first question that came Allegri’s way related to Kevin De Bruyne and his continued use in a deep midfield role. The Belgian has made it clear that he prefers to play further up the pitch where he is able to have more of an impact on attacking moves. VENICE, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli misses the penalty during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on October 17, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) When asked if he plans on using De Bruyne in the same position again, Allegri said: “These players have qualities and characteristics, he can play in front of the defence or in a double-pivot, I think he did that against Frosinone. I put him there and he played well, that’s the most important thing. “We also have players like Lobotka and Gilmour, who have played a lot of games since the start of the year between club and national teams. Managing the players is very important. When you play so many matches so close together, you need everyone. Today is our last training session, and then I will decide.” Just how important does Allegri feel tomorrow’s game against Roma is? VENICE, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Head coach of SSC Napoli Massimiliano Allegri during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on October 17, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) “It’s worth a lot, it’s an important game, it’s Napoli-Roma. Roma have been doing well since last year, they qualified for the Champions League, they’re near first place. Gasperini is doing a great job. They’re a team that’s playing with enthusiasm, good technique. “So it will be a difficult game but it would be nice to pick things back up after two wins and a draw before slipping against Venezia, while being aware of the fact that it is an important game, but not our last one, nor will it decide Champions League qualification. But, we are in eighth place and we have to improve in certain areas on the pitch.” Asked where he thinks Napoli need to improve, Allegri added: “Out of possession. We have to improve on that and we need continuity in results. We will only catch up by stringing a series of wins together.” And where do the dangers lie? “Gasperini’s teams make plays because they take you man for man, they create a lot of spaces. These can be beautiful and entertaining games, if you get the result. If not, it’s a problem. We need to have great technique, we will have to expend a lot of energy. Let’s see how we do in defence, everyone is all fine apart from Rrahmani, who had a fever, so we have to see how he is today.” ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Gian Piero Gasperini, Manager of AS Roma, looks on during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AS Roma and SK Slovan Bratislava at Stadio Olimpico on October 20, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) It was suggested that Gasperini’s side always have a clear identity and style of play, and that Napoli are missing exactly that under Allegri. In response, he said: ”The easiest way for me to respond would be to change my way, to abandon the defence and go all-out attack, but we need balance. We’ve needed that since the beginning. “The goal is to get all of our players back. We’ve got McTominay after two months out, he’s still a bit behind despite his two goals. Anguissa played 60 minutes and we have to see whether or not to deploy him because he only played 13 games last year and it takes a machine to be able to just switch it back on again. “We will also evaluate Vergara today to see if we can have him on the bench. I let Badiashile rest after playing three games in a row. Everyone is back in good condition but for some, they need to recover mentally as much as they do physically.” Allegri was then asked what he has made of Rasmus Hojlund’s recent form and lack of goals for Napoli. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Patrick Berg of FK Bodo/Glimt runs with the ball under pressure from Rasmus Hojlund of SSC Napoli during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) He said: “He went off to his national team, he had scored two in four of five games, then he scored a few for his national side, but he has played every game with Napoli and his national team since the start of the season, apart from that one game in Venice. But I’m happy with what he’s doing. He has to stay calm. The important thing is that the team scores. If Hojlund scores fewer goals but the team wins, we’re not angry. “Giovane is doing well, Lucca is someone with different qualities. We have to support and help him. Football is beautiful because one shot can turn a negative period into a positive.” Where does Allegri most want to see Napoli improve? “The main thing is that we give a stronger impression when we are out of possession, especially in our own half. We also have to make progress in terms of results. We can talk about having good games, but in the end, as we always say, we make our judgements on results.”

item.title: "We have the opportunity to win two consecutive games at home, and we must take advantage of this."
item.description: "We have the opportunity to win two consecutive games at home, and we must take advantage of this." The Girona coach, Quique Álvarez, appeared at a press conference ahead of the match the team will play tomorrow against Celta Fortuna at Montilivi. The coach emphasized the importance of maintaining good results at home, highlighted the internal competitiveness of the squad, and analyzed the main strengths of the opponent. One of the aspects the coach focused on was the need to maintain concentration and high standards to secure another victory in front of the fans. “Mentally, it is difficult to win two consecutive matches at home. We have worked on this. We cannot fall into that situation. We have a great opportunity to win two matches at home, and we must take advantage of it,” Álvarez stated, aware of the importance of maintaining a good dynamic at Montilivi. The coach also highlighted the role of competition among players in raising the collective level. “Internal competitiveness improves the team. One hundred percent,” he affirmed emphatically, emphasizing the importance of all players maintaining a high level of commitment to earn a spot in the starting eleven. Regarding the opponent, Álvarez warned of the challenges posed by the Galician team, a side with a clear playing style and quality players. “Celta Fortuna has very clear mechanisms, with physical and technical quality,” the coach explained, expecting a demanding match against an opponent with the resources to create problems. Finally, the coach was self-critical about some aspects of the team's play, particularly regarding the ability to create opportunities in central areas. “Surely, in recent matches, we have lacked play through the middle. But we have players to do it. They need to show their best version. In every match, we need to choose the players who can give us the most in this regard,” Álvarez pointed out, expressing confidence in the squad's ability to improve in this area and find the best solutions in each game.

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Europa League: Celtic lose to Celta after leading, Mateta returns in Palace draw
item.description: Sunderland drop points in 1-1 draw but stay unbeaten VAR rules out Juventus winner in draw with Rennes Celtic suffered more Europa League pain as Spanish side Celta Vigo came from behind to win 2-1 at Parkhead. After defeats by Ferencvaros and Benfica in their first two league phase fixtures, Martin O’Neill’s side struggled to impose themselves on the visitors who were neat and tidy without really testing Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone. Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half to thrill the Celtic fans but Spain defender Javi Rodríguez scored twice in three minutes – a header then an unstoppable drive – to stun the home side who could not find a way back. Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Next in line? Main contenders for the Manchester United hot seat
item.description: With Michael Carrick’s future at Old Trafford a matter of some debate, we examine the credentials of those who could succeed him The German was of interest to Manchester City while Omar Berrada was part of the hierarchy on the other side of town. He is highly thought of and would come with an impressive CV for a 39-year-old, having taken charge of Bayern Munich and Germany. Nagelsmann is regarded as an innovator who is very demanding of his players and builds teams to press relentlessly, a concept not currently used at United, as Bruno Fernandes will testify . His spell with Germany was underwhelming, concluding with a 2026 World Cup last-32 defeat by Paraguay , and at Bayern – with an exceptional squad – he won the Bundesliga in his only full season and was sacked the following March with the team second and still in the Champions League. item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
item.description: Bruno Fernandes followed Lisandro Martínez in revolt after his team’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago. And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie.
